places.name: 1921 Mount Dora
places.address: 1921 Mount Dora, 142 E 4th Ave, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5584
places.description: Dinner here feels like being welcomed into an elegant friend's home, in a house that explains why. 1921 Mount Dora pairs a historic 1921 home with modern Florida cuisine built on local farms. Order the Spanish octopus with hazelnut romesco, the wood-oven roasted oysters with BLT butter, and the Wagyu burger with smoked Duke's mayonnaise. The cooking treats Florida ingredients as a story worth telling well. Choose it for a Mount Dora evening that feels personal rather than formal, and book it for guests you want to impress quietly.

places.name: Amar Orlando
places.address: 8001 S Orange Blossom Trl, Ste #1510, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Fire and family recipes drive this Mediterranean kitchen, where shawarma comes shaved with intent. Amar serves olive oil that tastes like olives, pita warm enough to steam when you tear it and salads that crunch instead of wilt. The room runs on Levantine hospitality, feeding you like a guest rather than processing you like a transaction. When you want a bowl of food that leaves you feeling better than it found you, this is the stop. Simple details, handled properly, carry the whole meal.

places.name: Amare
places.address: Amare, 1255 Epcot Resorts Blvd, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: The Disney bubble dissolves at Amare into something calmer, older and built around the Mediterranean. Chef Scott West treats the region as a journey rather than a theme, moving from grilled coastal fish to slow, earthy braises. Each plate has a pour to match from a wine list built entirely around the region, and curated flights shortcut a tasting of Greece, Italy and Spain in one sitting. Ask about them. The rare resort restaurant here earns the trip on its own merits.

places.name: American Social
places.address: 7335 W Sand Lake Rd Ste 101, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: American Social is where Restaurant Row lets its hair down. Equal parts sports bar, restaurant and live-music stage, it runs on high voltage: big screens in every sightline, a bar pouring hand-crafted cocktails and local beer, and a kitchen that treats bar food like it matters, burgers with actual char, croquetas worth ordering twice. Regulars mix with first-timers from the theme parks, and the room is built for that exact collision, conversations you didn't plan and nights that run later than intended.

places.name: Aphrodisiaco
places.address: 8267 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Romance is designed into the lighting, the music, and the plate at Aphrodisiaco. Named for the goddess of love, this I-Drive speakeasy keeps light warm and low and music close without drowning conversation. The kitchen thinks in elements, fire, sea, and earth, with handcrafted cocktails built to match the mood of each dish. Make this the reservation when the night matters and you want every sense leaned into the evening. Dress well, because the room quietly expects the same effort from you.

places.name: Bacán
places.address: Bacán, 6100 Wave Hotel Dr, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Dinner at Bacan begins in an open theater kitchen, where the cooking is part of the night. Chef Guillaume Robin, honored as a Maitre Cuisinier de France, works with Sous Chef Ryne Wood in Lake Nona. Their menu draws on flavors from across the Americas, led by whole Florida snapper. Save room for the banana tart finished with gold leaf and the chocolate sphere that melts open at your table. Book it for an elevated night that still feels approachable and unexpected.

places.name: Banh Mi Boy
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Michelin handed it a Bib Gourmand and Netflix's Somebody Feed Phil came with cameras, but Banh Mi Boy never changed its tune. A Mills Market fixture serving for over twenty years, it bakes baguettes that shatter the way Saigon street bread should, then loads them with crispy pork belly, roasted garlic mayo and house pate. The playful side shows in the pho French dip, a sandwich built for dunking in rich broth, and fresh-pressed sugarcane juice. For Vietnamese sandwiches in Mills 50, this is the benchmark regulars measure others against.

places.name: Banh Mi Cali
places.address: Banh Mi Cali, 5210 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32808-7606
places.description: No frills, no pretense, just one of Orlando's most honest banh mi counters in Mills 50. The sandwiches come on crisp, airy baguettes stuffed with the classics: roast pork, meatballs, house pate and terrine, with pickled carrot and daikon crunching through every bite. Regulars round it out with a strong Vietnamese iced coffee or a milk tea, and the doughnuts earn their own quiet reputation. Small and fast, it is exactly the kind of unassuming lunch spot locals protect, best when you want the sandwich to do all the talking.

places.name: Beefy King
places.address: Beefy King, 424 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803-6028
places.description: Orlando defends this counter the way cities defend institutions, because lunch here has history. Since 1968, Freeman and Margaret Smith's shop on Bumby Avenue has steamed roast beef until it falls apart, then piled it onto soft steamed kaiser rolls with diced onions. Beefy Spuds, crisp tater tots by another name, and chili that tastes like decades of practice complete the order. The shop survived an arson fire and came back swinging. Choose Beefy King for lunch, and you understand why the drive thru chain version gets ignored here.

places.name: Black Bean Deli
places.address: 1835 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A Cuban cafe built from family memory still cooks like the grandparents are watching. Owner Andres Corton drew on his grandparents' kitchen and the ventanita culture of 1960s Miami cafes for this Mills 50 deli. Pan con lechon arrives stacked with mojo kissed pulled pork, empanadas crackle with seasoned picadillo, and the guava pastelito stays flaky without turning cloying. Order cafe con leche strong and sweet, made for sharing. Cuban families in Orlando point here when the standard is home cooking.

places.name: Blue Man Group
places.address: Blue Man Theater at ICON Park, 8390 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Paint drums splatter in rhythm, tubes thump overhead, and without a word three blue performers pull the audience into the joke. Blue Man Group plays in its new custom theater at ICON Park on I-Drive, a wordless mix of drums, paint, and participation for all ages. It fits most groups: bring kids or grandparents, sit back from the splash zone, and stay out at ICON Park after. Tourist Trail: Worth it: a fresh room for a show that still works.

places.name: Bombay Street Kitchen
places.address: 6215 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando
places.description: Forget the tired curry-house playbook. Bombay Street Kitchen, from chef Amit Kumar of the beloved Aashirwad and Tamarind, is a love letter to the street carts of Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai and Bangalore, and Michelin noticed, awarding it a Bib Gourmand. The menu reads like a food tour: Dahi Bhalla Papri Chaat with its tangle of tangy, crunchy, cool; crispy Kurkuri Bhindi Bhel with pomegranate popping through; tandoori momos with real char. Save room for the falooda, rose syrup, vermicelli and rabdi in a glass. This is India beyond the clichés, on Orange Blossom Trail.

places.name: Boxi Park Lake Nona
places.address: 6877 Tavistock Lakes Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Forty foot shipping containers became Lake Nona's open air party, and the idea works. Boxi Park stacks the boxes into a hangout where you graze lobster rolls from Claw and Order, tacos from Canonita and housemade burgers while a live band plays. A pup park handles the dog, beach volleyball handles the restless, and rotating pop ups under the Before It's Gone banner keep the lineup moving. Drinks come from Bar Nona and Hops and Vine. Bring everyone, because the format suits everyone.

places.name: Briarpatch
places.address: Briarpatch Restaurant, 252 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-3814
places.description: Park Avenue breakfast has an institution, and Briarpatch has held that role since 1980. Owner John Pertz, a French Culinary Institute graduate, runs the kitchen on brioche baked in house with honey and lemon zest, premium olive oil, and clarified butter instead of shortcuts. Avocados get chosen with obsessive care by the kitchen. Famous French toast comes stuffed with raspberry and brie, pancakes wear raspberry lemon cream, and short rib Benedict has ruined lesser Benedicts for generations of Rollins students. Choose the covered patio for Winter Park at its most civilized, and take peanut butter pie home.

places.name: Buttermilk Bakery
places.address: Buttermilk Bakery, 1198 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4908
places.description: Every layer in the case shows the early work behind it. Buttermilk Bakery is the Rebroff family's tribute to European baking, run by Lana with her children Phillip, Taissa, and Alex in Winter Park. Small batch croissants shatter as they should, and the case rotates with the seasons: pumpkin cheesecake croissants in fall, strawberry rhubarb tarts in spring, plus brioche donuts and savory khachapuri. Get there before the devoted regulars do, because the strongest trays sell out.

places.name: Camille
places.address: Camille, 4962 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6415
places.description: Chef Tung Phan named his Baldwin Park restaurant for his eldest daughter and cooks like he is honoring the name. Camille earned a Michelin star for a singular vision: the food culture of Vietnam presented in a refined, progressive form, with French technique woven through every course. The eight-seat chef's counter is theater, with pho reimagined through wagyu tartare and savory broth, and red bean desserts that play like a cheese course. It started as a pop-up, and the daring never left. For a milestone night, few Orlando rooms feel this considered.

places.name: Capa
places.address: 10100 Dream Tree Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Seventeen floors up inside the Four Seasons, Capa makes a case that the great steakhouse tradition belongs to Spain too. Chefs Fabrizio Schenardi and Chris Edwards cook over a wood-burning grill in an open kitchen, sending out Wagyu from Florida's own Clear Creek Farm alongside tapas that show off: fried cauliflower with capers and a fried egg, pork cheeks with Marcona almonds. Start with cocktails on the rooftop terrace, where the view stretches over golf greens and wetlands to the nightly Disney fireworks. Dark wood, black and crimson, candlelight, the whole romantic apparatus, earned.

places.name: Casa Mezcal
places.address: 8267 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The spirit is the headliner on International Drive, and the kitchen knows how to back it up. Casa Mezcal pours mezcal and tequila with conviction from a full bar, builds tacos for proper pairings and leans festive after the sun goes down. Music and conversation fill the room as dinner slides into drinks without anyone formally deciding to stay. Dress up a little and come hungry. Pick it when a late night Mexican room, not a quick taco stop, is the plan.

places.name: Cañonita
places.address: 6877 Tavistock Lakes Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: A Venetian born brand brings Mexico City street food to Lake Nona in two forms. Canonita began at The Venetian in Las Vegas with canal front dining and a deep tequila list. In Lake Nona, the walk up Street Taqueria inside Boxi Park serves street tacos, nachos and chips with salsa under string lights, while the full service Canonita at Lake Nona West is run by the Tavistock Restaurant Collection. Grab tacos, a margarita from the Boxi Park bar and let the crew order differently.

places.name: Celine Orlando
places.address: 22 S Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown's answer to where the night goes when it wants options has three floors on Magnolia Avenue. Celine stacks a Prohibition-era speakeasy below, a grand ballroom with chandeliers and full-throttle light design in the middle, and a rooftop lounge where DJs play to open sky and the downtown towers. Craft cocktails flow across all three levels, and the crowd is a downtown mix: concerts one night, DJ sets the next, celebrations always. Pick your floor, or wander between them all as the night changes.

places.name: Charles Hosmer Morse Museum of American Art
places.address: 445 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Modest from the street, breathtaking inside: the Morse holds a comprehensive collection of Louis Comfort Tiffany in Winter Park. Hugh and Jeannette McKean salvaged truckloads of art and architecture from Tiffany's fire-ravaged Long Island estate and brought it here, including the Byzantine-Romanesque chapel interior built for Chicago's 1893 World's Columbian Exposition. Lamps, leaded-glass windows and iridescent vases shift color as you move through the galleries. People make pilgrimages for this material, and standing in the rooms you understand why. It is the anchor of Winter Park's arts claim.

places.name: Chathams Place
places.address: Chatham's Place, 7575 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-5149
places.description: Old-school fine dining survives in this Dr. Phillips dining room, and that is exactly the point. Chatham's Place is independently owned, chef-driven, and unapologetically classic: Chef Tony's kitchen sends out lobster salad, center-cut filet and off-menu treasures like pesto Parmesan pasta twirled tableside inside a whole wheel of cheese. A live pianist fills the dim, intimate room, and the service treats anniversaries like the sacred occasions they are. This is where Orlando's special nights have been going for nearly thirty years.

places.name: Chef Mickey's
places.address: Chef Mickey's, 4600 N World Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830-8413
places.description: Some Disney memories are manufactured, but the joy in this room is real. Chef Mickey's sits on the Contemporary Resort's grand concourse, monorail gliding right through the building, and every meal is a celebration: Mickey, Minnie, Goofy, Pluto and Donald working the tables while the whole room twirls napkins overhead to music. The buffet does the heavy lifting, breakfast spreads and dinner carving stations built for refills and second plates. For a kid meeting Mickey Mouse up close, there is no substitute. Book early, the world knows about this one.

places.name: Coro
places.address: Coro, 3022 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2204
places.description: The name means chorus, and the menu sings in one voice. Chef Tim Lovero's Audubon Park restaurant earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand for small plates that change with the seasons and the chef's mood: warm potato naan with whipped chicken skin butter and marmalade, lamb shoulder so tender it surrenders, and a dessert riffing on fries and a milkshake with panna cotta, crispy sunchoke and cocoa nibs. The open kitchen puts the cooks within arm's reach, and the wine list leans natural. Choose it for intimate, evolving cooking at its best.

places.name: Cowboy Curry
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: From the UniGirl family comes a love letter to Japanese curry done the slow way: forty hours, forty ingredients, and a sauce sweetened only with fruits and vegetables, no gluten, no dairy, just depth. The base curry is beef, slow-cooked to silk, and then you build: chicken katsu with real crunch, gyu katsu, fried karaage, fried oyster. The bowl arrives deep and steaming, and a cup of hojicha tea on the side is the move. Comfort food with an obsession behind it, in the middle of Mills Market's chaos.

places.name: Cups and Pups
places.address: 2413 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: A roadside cart grew into an airstream, then into a bright Edgewater Drive shop, without losing its charm. Cups and Pups builds its menu on joy: a Honey Nut Cheerio Latte that tastes like the bottom of the cereal bowl, a Brown Sugar Pop Tart Latte, and lavender cold brew. Rotating seasonal creations use Lineage Coffee as the base for the drinks. The dog friendly patio lets you order from your seat without leaving your pup, and the dog face logo cutout inside invites photos. Choose it for a laptop friendly, tail friendly College Park ritual.

places.name: Domu
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Since November 2016, Domu has been the ramen room Orlando talks about. The East End Market original earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand and a Netflix spotlight, and the bowls live up to it. Start with the kimchi butter wings, then the Richie Rich ramen, and give yourself over to the broth. The room is compact, the line is real, and first come, first served keeps the energy honest. It is worth the wait for ramen drinkers who plan around a bowl, especially on a first visit to Audubon Park.

places.name: Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts
places.address: 445 S Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: For decades Orlando proved it could fill stadiums, but nobody knew if it could fill a concert hall night after night. Then Dr. Phillips Center opened in 2014 and answered that question for good. Broadway tours light up the Walt Disney Theater, Steinmetz Hall pours out symphony sound with pristine acoustics, and the Judson's Live cabaret room keeps the late nights intimate. This is the two block stretch where Orlando found its cultural heartbeat.

places.name: Edoboy
places.address: 728 N Thornton Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Eight seats, no chairs, and twelve pieces at a standing counter: Edoboy is Orlando's first standing sushi bar. Chef Sean "Sonny" Nguyen built the passion project after travels through Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto, where standing sushi is a local shortcut to excellence. You book a slot on Resy, stand at the counter, and order nigiri and hand rolls from the chefs piece by piece, each one brushed and ready. Finish with miso soup made from the fish bones of the day and, wisely, the matcha s'more. Fast, fun, and fiercely good, it rewards planning.

places.name: El Cilantrillo
places.address: El Cilantrillo Restaurant, 1301 Florida Mall Ave, Orlando, FL 32809-7731
places.description: Orlando's Puerto Rican community has a big table, and El Cilantrillo sets it in South Orlando. Mofongo arrives stuffed and towering, the chuleta kan kan comes massive, churrasco comes off the plancha, and arroz con gandules tastes closely watched. Live salsa music rolls through the dining room, coconut mojitos carry a reputation, and Don Turull Cafe pours island coffee dedicated to the founder's father. Start here when you want Puerto Rican comfort served in full color and full portions.

places.name: Enzo's On the Lake
places.address: Enzo's on the Lake, 1130 S US Highway 17 92, Longwood, FL 32750-5718
places.description: On the shore of Lake Kathryn in Longwood, Enzo's has been Central Florida's special-occasion Italian since 1980, and it has only gotten better at the job. The dining room glows warm, the La Terrazza deck sits right at the water for sunset, and the kitchen cooks with old-world confidence: bucatini alla Enzo, Dover sole that regulars swear is the finest they've had anywhere, a wine list deep enough to get lost in. Live music drifts across the lake after dinner. Some restaurants are meals; this one is an evening.

places.name: EPCOT
places.address: 200 Epcot Center Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Walt's grandest what-if still stands at Disney. EPCOT opened in 1982 as the Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow, his World's Fair dream of a city of the future, and four neighborhoods carry that ambition now: celebration, discovery, nature and the World Showcase, where eleven countries ring a lagoon. Come during a festival, Flower and Garden in spring or Food and Wine in fall, when the park becomes one long global tasting menu, and stay for the nighttime spectacular over the water. It is Disney's most curiosity-driven park.

places.name: Everoak Farm
places.address: Everoak Farm, 2335 Carrington Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: Three acres, ten minutes from downtown, are growing food the slow and deliberate way. Husband and wife team Mike and Nikki Garcia run Everoak as a regenerative, biointensive family farm with no sprays, bees working the rows and pasture raised chickens roaming. Certified Naturally Grown produce comes from living soil, and their Saturday market gathers fellow small businesses beside the farm stand. Their CSA feeds seventy local families, and harvests reach restaurant menus across town. Start here to taste where Orlando farm to table begins.

places.name: Fat One's Hot Dogs & Italian Ice
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Yes, that Joey Fatone, and the hot dogs go well beyond ballpark fare. The *NSYNC member and Orlando native opened a permanent CityWalk restaurant with longtime manager Joe Mulvihill, and the menu loads nine creations. The Fat One buries a footlong under roasted pork, pepperoni, chili beans, cheddar cheese sauce, and pop fries. The Brazilian pairs grilled linguica with Calabrian honey and jalapeno veganaise, while the Dirty K-Pop Dog adds kimchi slaw and gochujang mayo. Cool down with old school Italian ice and a specialty beer for pure Orlando pop culture joy.

places.name: Flatlands Bar & Grill
places.address: 124 Ruby Red Place, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Brand new at Flamingo Crossings, and already worth leaving the Disney bubble for. From restaurateur Nick Valenti with executive chef Dominique Filoni, formerly of Disney's Cítricos and Topolino's Terrace, Flatlands is built around Central Florida's 1920s citrus boom: the building looks like a vintage packing facility, and the cooking follows the Italian-immigrant principles behind it, great ingredients, simple preparations, zero compromise. The Maine lobster rolls are the breakout star, the cookie skillet finishes strong, and the Orange Blossom Collins drinks like Florida itself. Disney-adjacent dining, all grown up.

places.name: Foreigner Restaurant
places.address: Foreigner Restaurant, 2816 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2226
places.description: Chef Bruno Fonseca's Brazilian roots run through this Corrine Drive counter like a current. Foreigner is a chef's-counter tasting room serving a menu confiance, a monthly-changing parade of globally inspired courses, where poached oysters meet caviar and brown butter powder, mackerel gets the moqueca treatment, and picanha lands with bordelaise and morels. It began as intimate popups, and the intimacy survived the move to a permanent room: Chef Bruno introduces each course personally, the wine pairings are chosen with real care, and you leave feeling like a houseguest who was fussed over beautifully.

places.name: Four Flamingos
places.address: Four Flamingos, 1 Grand Cypress Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Chef Richard Blais brought his first Florida kitchen to the Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress, playful from the start. Four Flamingos pairs an open kitchen, a raw bar, and a live lobster tank with a dining room the record calls a tropical oasis. The menu chases Florida's bounty: Tuna Tostada crowned with a passion fruit yolk, bone-in swordfish prime rib, and coconut and mango running through dishes. Order the Key Lime in the Coconut cocktail. Stay for laid-back energy when a Disney-area dinner should linger rather than rush.

places.name: Francesco's Ristorante
places.address: Francesco's Ristorante, 400 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Palermo-born chef Francesco Aiello trained at Sicily's prestigious Istituto Alberghiero, opened his Maitland namesake in 2012, and just swept five awards, including Best Italian in Florida and Best Local Chef. The proof is in the open flame: wood-burning ovens blister hand-tossed Margheritas, pastas are rolled by hand, mozzarella is made in-house, and the kitchen turns out gnocchi Siciliana, spaghetti alle vongole, and a tableside Pinwheel Reggiano Flambéed Pappardella that is pure theater. Chef Francesco plates in the open kitchen and works the room like family. This is Maitland's pride, and it eats like it.

places.name: Fluffy Fluffy Dessert Cafe
places.address: 2008 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Fuwa fuwa means fluffy fluffy in Japanese, and each pancake keeps that promise. Fluffy Fluffy Dessert Cafe was founded by Benson Lau, and the Mills 50 shop helped the jiggly obsession take hold. Each souffle pancake is made to order: egg whites whipped to soft peaks, cooked low and slow until it wobbles like a cloud. Tiramisu, creme brulee, and matcha white chocolate arrive theatrical and disappear fast. Save this stop for when happiness is the entire agenda, and give the kitchen time to cook properly.

places.name: Gideon's Bakehouse (Disney Springs Flagship)
places.address: 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A line in Disney Springs usually signals hype, but these cookies carry real weight. Steve Lewis started baking in his kitchen before Gideon's Bakehouse grew into a candlelit, Victorian style room where a gargoyle guards the case. The cookies are nearly half pound, handmade, and take more than 24 hours to prepare, with the Original Chocolate Chip converting plenty of skeptics. Cake slices and serious cold brew widen the order. Go early and hungry, and expect the wait to be part of the ritual.

faqs.q: Do you need reservations for Gideon's Bakehouse?
faqs.a: No reservations - it's a virtual queue. Expect ~2 hours on weekdays and up to ~5 on weekends. Go during Hot Cookie Hours (2-3 PM and 7-8 PM); there's a 7-cookie limit.

faqs.q: How do I skip the Gideon's line?
faqs.a: You can't skip it, but sister savory spot Six Ravens next door at The Landing usually has a much shorter wait.

places.name: Golden Hour Wine
places.address: Golden Hour Wine, 1560 Lake Baldwin Ln, Orlando, FL 32814-6661
places.description: Owner Heather named the shop for her favorite time to drink wine in Florida. Golden Hour Wine is a woman owned neighborhood shop and bar in Baldwin Park stocking roughly 700 bottles of responsibly farmed, small production natural wine. The selection leans proudly toward women producers, grower Champagne, German Riesling, and alpine and island wines. Something is always open for tasting, and staff match a bottle to your mood, not just your menu. Sip in the cozy shop or take the sunset home.

places.name: Grocery Los Hermanos
places.address: 4130 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Buy your chiles, watch the butcher case, then sit down for tacos that shame dedicated shops. Grocery Los Hermanos on Curry Ford is a family owned market and taqueria in East Orlando. Carne asada and al pastor tacos arrive on fresh handmade tortillas, verde enchiladas carry a kick locals return for, and aguas frescas stay ice cold. The dining corner is bright and art filled. Grocery first and restaurant by destiny, it is exactly the kind of place Orlando runs on daily.

places.name: Harlow Grove
places.address: 186 S Main St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Downtown Winter Garden's new social headquarters sits beneath a century-old oak, two stories of curated warmth where nobody checks the time. From the Knallhart Management Group, Harlow Grove runs on the philosophy of staying awhile: the downstairs bar hums with handcrafted cocktails like the Eden Spritz and HG Espresso Martini, the upstairs dining room serves comfort food with ambition, short rib dip, heirloom burrata, baby back ribs, lobster lasagna. The open-air terrace overlooks the town. Come for a weekday bite and accidentally stay through the night.

places.name: Hillstone Winter Park
places.address: Hillstone Restaurant, 215 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-3657
places.description: Locals still call it Houston's, but whatever the sign says, this lakeside room on Lake Killarney is Winter Park's dependable special night table. Every seat faces the water, the sunsets do the decorating, and the family run kitchen works a wood burning grill on American classics: the Hawaiian ribeye regulars plan weeks around, a French dip with a cult following, and spinach and artichoke dip that arrives bubbling. The name comes from a Napa Valley vineyard. Time your visit for golden hour on the lake and you understand the devotion.

places.name: House of Blues
places.address: 1490 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Disney Springs' West Side rock club has carried a Southern accent since 1997. The House of Blues Music Hall is general admission and standing room, which keeps you close enough to feel the drum hits, and the calendar runs rock, hip hop, country, Latin, blues and tribute nights. Come early for Crossroads and eat shrimp and grits or jambalaya under the folk art of Mr. Imagination, then catch the gospel brunch on Sunday. It suits concertgoers who want dinner and a show in one stop.

places.name: Hunger Street Tacos
places.address: Hunger Street Tacos, 2103 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4507
places.description: A Fairbanks Avenue corner in Winter Park became a pilgrimage site for taco lovers, one bite at a time. Brothers Joe and David Creech built Hunger Street as a tribute to La Calle del Hambre in Mexico City. Their menu writes that tribute in tender suadero on heirloom corn tortillas, tamal soaked in deep red mole and a fried avocado taco that converts skeptics. Murals cover the walls inside and out, and outdoor seating hums. You taste a family feeding you the recipes they grew up with.

places.name: ICON Park & The Orlando Eye
places.address: 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The whole I-Drive night skyline has a new compass point. ICON Park's 400 foot wheel lifts you above the city for a slow soar with Orlando spread out in every direction, and the ground below keeps the energy going: the SEA LIFE ocean tunnel, Madame Tussauds, live music at Tin Roof, and SlingShot launching the brave 450 feet straight up. No gates and no ticket to wander in, just a park that keeps giving you reasons to stay into the evening.

places.name: Barbarella Orlando
places.address: 2600 Lee Rd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Downtown Orlando's clubhouse for people who still buy records and argue about setlists is Barbarella on Orange Avenue. A gritty, multi-level live music den, it spins its calendar through themed nights, tribute bands, karaoke and all the flavors of loud guitar. The crowd shows up the way they always have: sleeves up, all in. Multiple bars and dance floors keep the energy circulating, and the sound system earns its keep. The whole place runs on a loyalty you cannot buy, which is exactly why regulars protect it.

places.name: Jaleo
places.address: Jaleo, 1482 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830-8518
places.description: A celebrity chef restaurant that eats like a love letter to Spain anchors Disney Springs. Jose Andres built Jaleo here with jamon sliced thin enough to glisten, tapas that taste like a Madrid night out and wood fired paellas layered with saffron and garlic aioli. Rumba guitarists roam on Sundays, the Matador Bar runs a sangria hour, and Pepe next door serves bocatas for the grab and go version. A group dinner feels like a celebration without losing the cooking.

places.name: Jiang's Kitchen
places.address: 27 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: You watch dinner get folded here, pleat by pleat, before the broth hits your spoon. Eric Jiang brought this downtown newcomer to the Arts District with soup dumplings made by hand in an open kitchen. The first bite releases rich broth over delicate pork, beef, shrimp, or crab, turning a casual weeknight into a memory. Around the dumplings, authentic Shanghai cooking and sushi sit beside a full bar. The owner comes from a family that already runs respected Asian kitchens in the area. Choose Jiang's for dumpling theater with substance behind the show.

places.name: Juju
places.address: 700 Maguire Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Do not let the converted Pizza Hut roofline fool you: inside this oddity is an exciting Japanese room. Juju shares the same playful spirit as its sibling Susuru but raises the game, an izakaya menu for the adventurous, and a tiny kappo counter where the chefs build original kaiseki-style courses. Dry-aged sashimi is the revelation, two-week-aged king salmon and otoro finished with Kaluga caviar tasting deeper than you thought fish could. The chawanmushi arrives crowned with lobster head dashi, pure theater. Booking the counter is the move, and you will talk about it for weeks.

places.name: Kabooki Sushi
places.address: Kabooki Sushi, 7705 Turkey Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-5221
places.description: Ask any serious sushi lover in Orlando to name the room that leveled up the whole scene and this name comes up first. Chef Henry Moso leads Kabooki with a restless, globe-trotting approach: meticulous Japanese technique with creative freedom to borrow from everywhere, plated with genuine artistry. The traditional kaiseki multi-course option is the deep end, while the broader menu rewards adventurous ordering with combinations you will not see twice. The lounge out back keeps things sultry, and the whole place hums with the confidence of a restaurant that has stayed at the top by never repeating itself.

places.name: Kabooki Sushi Downtown
places.address: 3122 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The Kabooki name carries serious weight in Orlando, and the downtown location brings that reputation to the city center. Same philosophy: chef-driven sushi with meticulous technique and a creative streak that pulls from beyond Japan, served in a room built for a night out. The kaiseki multi-course experience remains the connoisseur's move, the rolls and crudos deliver spectacle and precision in equal measure, and the lounge energy means this is as much a downtown evening destination as it is a dinner. When the occasion matters, Orlando trusts Kabooki.

places.name: Kadence
places.address: 1809 Winter Park Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A tiny counter, a Michelin star, and the room where Orlando's sushi dreams come true. What started in 2014 as a tiny sushi stand in Audubon Park has grown into a decorated Florida dining room, where the owners' Michelin training and certified sake expertise shape a secret omakase that changes with the seasons. Each course lands in front of you, beautifully plated and built for the brave, fatty tuna, yuzu pepper scallops, whatever the chefs are obsessed with this week. Intimate, romantic, and worth every minute of the wait for a reservation.

places.name: Kaya
places.address: 618 N Thornton Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Filipino cooking gets a personal, farm-linked treatment in Mills 50, where Chef Lordfer Lalicon and Jamilyn Salonga Bailey run Kaya as casual fine dining. Lalicon, a veteran of Michelin-starred kitchens including Blue Hill, applies Filipino techniques to Florida farms and waters. Seafood and vegetable-focused plates carry the color, while ube pancakes and adobo fried rice keep tables smiling. The room feels like a family dinner filtered through very good taste. You leave understanding why Orlando took to this kitchen so quickly.

places.name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs Run
places.address: 400 E Kelly Park Rd, Apopka, FL 32712
places.description: A short drive out, Florida hands you its finest natural water park at Kelly Park. Rock Springs pours out of the earth in a clear channel that looks lit from within, and the tubing run downstream is among the laziest half hours you can spend in Central Florida. Dr. Howard Kelly, a Johns Hopkins founder, gave this land to the people of Apopka in 1927, and it still feels like a gift. Paddle the Emerald Cut for jungle-walled seclusion, watch for turtles and otters, then hike. On a hot day, little else competes.

faqs.q: What time should I arrive at Kelly Park / Rock Springs?
faqs.a: Line up by 5-6:30 AM on summer weekends - the park issues ~280 morning entry vouchers and regularly hits capacity before 9 AM. Entry is $3-5 per car; bring your own tube or rent on site.

places.name: Kia Center (formerly Amway Center)
places.address: 400 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Orlando's beating heart sits at Church Street. The Kia Center, home of the Orlando Magic and the Solar Bears, is the arena that anchored downtown's revival, and Magic fans keep voting it one of the NBA's best game night experiences. Beyond basketball and hockey, major touring acts stop here, and the building itself rewards a look, with hundreds of works of art woven through its concourses. Whether you bleed Magic blue or just want the roar of a sold out show, this is the room where the city gathers loudest.

places.name: King Bao
places.address: 710 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Mills 50 has a hole-in-the-wall hero, and it serves steamed buns with attitude. King Bao claims an early quick-service gourmet bao title in Orlando, then backs the attitude with a rule-breaking menu. The pork-belly Hogzilla, zesty Firecracker Shrimp, a Cuban bao, Nashville hot chicken with real fire, and crispy Fire tots fill the board. Early-2000s metal rattles the speakers, wall art keeps things trippy, and a self-serve kiosk keeps the line moving. Come for loud, inexpensive bao that feels genuinely fun rather than formulaic.

places.name: Knife & Spoon
places.address: Knife & Spoon, 4012 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32837-7662
places.description: A Ritz-Carlton Grande Lakes dining room helped put Orlando fine dining on the Michelin map, built by Chef John Tesar around a simple split: knife for beef, spoon for seafood. Tesar, a two-time Top Chef contestant, was called by Bourdain the most talented cook he ever worked with. Steaks dry-age for weeks or even months until the flavor turns nutty and deep, while seafood spans Florida catches and Japanese imports. The tuna and foie gras appetizer is well known. Elegant without stiffness, the room suits skeptics and celebrants alike.

places.name: Kres Chophouse
places.address: Kres Chophouse, 17 Church St W, Orlando, FL 32801-3301
places.description: Inside a 1930s Church Street landmark with original architecture to match, Kres has been downtown's power-steakhouse for years, and it wears the title with swagger. Prime beef is aged in-house and hand-cut to order, the Filet Wellington arrives flawless, and daily Florida coastal fish keeps the seafood side honest. There is even a full vegan menu, oysters Rockefeller included, which tells you how confident this kitchen is. Walkable from the Kia Center and Dr. Phillips, it is the classic pre-show or special-occasion move.

places.name: Kung Fu Kitchen
places.address: Kungfu Kitchen, 8466 Palm Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32836-6431
places.description: Soup dumpling obsession starts with noodles and bao made the hard way. Kung Fu Kitchen, a Flushing, New York export, built its Orlando following on hand pulled ramen and knife cut noodles that land springy and fresh in soup or stir fried. Xiao long bao arrive delicate and soup filled with pork, chicken, or crab, and pan fried Shanghai pork buns quiet the table. Chocolate xiao long bao tastes like cake batter in dumpling form. Choose the red walled, booth lined room when a noodle run deserves planning across town.

places.name: Lake Eola Park & Linton E. Allen Memorial Fountain
places.address: Lake Eola Park, 512 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801-1941
places.description: The lake Orlando sees in its dreams sits in the middle of downtown. Swans glide past the paddle boats at Lake Eola, the fountain throws light and water into the skyline, and the 0.9 mile loop around the shore might be the most walked path in the city. Come for a slow stroll, stay for a concert in the Walt Disney Amphitheater, and linger for the Sunday farmers market. Few places gather a whole city the way this park does, which makes it downtown's default meeting ground.

faqs.q: How much are the swan boats at Lake Eola, and when are they open?
faqs.a: Swan pedal boats run about $15 for 30 minutes, Tuesday-Sunday 10 AM-7 PM (closed Mondays), no reservations - first come, first served. A rainbow boat joined the fleet in June 2026.

places.name: Level 99
places.address: 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Forget what you thought you knew about the old NBA Experience building at Disney Springs. Level99 packs a warehouse of life sized mini games, from axe dodging beams to logic puzzles to head to head duels, all unlocked by an RFID wristband at check in, and the record calls it the largest interactive gaming playground of its kind in the country. Team up for cooperative challenge rooms, settle scores in duels, or hunt through the art scavenger hunt. The bar pours craft cocktails and local beers, and the scratch kitchen's Detroit style pizza fuels rounds.

places.name: Lukes Kitchen and Bar
places.address: Luke's Kitchen and Bar, 640 Orlando Ave S, Maitland, FL 32751-5612
places.description: Maitland gets its everyday celebration here. From the team behind Winter Park's Luma on Park and Prato, Luke's is chef Brandon McGlamery's love letter to classic American cooking with a playful brain. The blackened fish collar and Cheshire pork chop over goat cheese boursin grits are the signatures, PB&J spare ribs and a towering shellfish starter keep the adventurous happy, and locals insist the patio is the finest in Maitland. Craft cocktails use house made ingredients. It earns its regulars, and it will likely earn you.

places.name: Luminescent
places.address: Luminescent, 12286 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32826-4709
places.description: East Orlando's day-to-night dream. Luminescent runs a dual life that actually works: a polished, Indian-influenced coffee bar by day, a craft cocktail lounge after dark, all wrapped around a deep-green bar in a room people call impeccable. The drinks are where it gets special, a Keral's Kulfi built on pistachio cold foam and soan papdi, traditional chā, affogatos with real kulfi ice cream, plus pistachio, cardamom, and rose water weaving through both the espresso and the cocktails. Come in the morning to work, come back at night to unwind. A rare two-visit place.

places.name: Magic Kingdom Park
places.address: Disney's Magic Kingdom, 1180 Seven Seas Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: You know this park before you ever set foot in it, and it still gets you. Cinderella Castle stands at the hub of six lands, with Space Mountain's rattling darkness, the Haunted Mansion's stretching rooms and pirates singing their song: rides that double as shared memories the country grew up with. Locals come back for the fireworks, the Festival of Fantasy parade and watching a child's first visit through their own eyes. Plan for a full day, walk Main Street slowly, and give in to the place completely.

places.name: Mango's Tropical Cafe
places.address: Mango's Tropical Cafe, 8126 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-9323
places.description: Dinner, a show and a dance floor were never separate plans at Mango's. The International Drive supper club rebuilt what its South Beach Ocean Drive original learned, only bigger, and the legend grew with the room. You eat under live Latin music, dancers and handcrafted cocktails, then the building turns fully into a nightclub as the night deepens. Ask anyone who came for dinner and stayed to close. Choose Mango's when the group wants one address to carry the entire evening.

places.name: Mecatos
places.address: 610 W Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Colombian coffee gets flown in for the cup, and the bakery case explains the rest. Mecatos, Orlando's Colombian gathering place, roasts beans sourced straight from Colombia for a taste of the highlands. The Winter Park room on Morse Boulevard serves warm pan de bono with a cheese pull, crispy empanadas, guava and cheese pastries and a strawberry napoleon regulars rave about. A covered patio makes lingering easy, and the kitchen runs breakfast through dinner. Orlando's Colombian community has made it theirs for good reason.

places.name: Mengs Kitchen
places.address: Meng's Kitchen, 2415 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5018
places.description: The best seat in the house, regulars say, is inside a grocery store on East Colonial. Meng's Kitchen sits in the back of iFresh Market, a tiny stall cooking soulful Southeast Asian food. The Hainan chicken and rice combo, poached and fried, is the move; the five-spice roasted chicken and golden crispy pork belly have real devotees, and the katsu curry and panang oxtail keep things bold. Seating is tiny, so take it to go and eat well at home. Street-food flavor with home-kitchen heart defines the stall.

places.name: Mohawk Smokehouse
places.address: 480 S Ronald Reagan Blvd, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: A cook who learned beside his Italian grandmother now draws critics for Texas style brisket. Tyler Evans and his wife Sarah launched Mohawk Smokehouse in 2022, calling their approach craft BBQ with southern roots. The brisket carries serious bark and marbling, Southern comfort shows up in shrimp and grits, and ingredients are fresh and locally sourced, with a Critic's Choice nod for Orlando barbecue to the name. Mohawk runs pop-ups, events, and catering, so chase the schedule when brisket is the mission.

places.name: Morimoto Asia
places.address: Morimoto Asia, 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: The grand opening set a theatrical tone that the room still carries. Morimoto Asia retells that opening with Morimoto himself cracking a sake cask and turning a large tuna into a long maki roll. A decade later, the two-story Disney Springs dining hall remains striking, serving the chef's first pan-Asian menu through dim sum, pristine sushi, and a bar program built around sake, including sake sangria. The kitchen and prep space reportedly run bigger than the dining room. Choose it for polished, theatrical pan-Asian cooking.

places.name: Mosonori
places.address: Mosonori, 7541 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-5109
places.description: Chef Henry Moso, the genius behind Kabooki, did something radical for the I-Drive corridor: he opened a handroll bar. Mosonori on Sand Lake is all about temaki, one handroll at a time, served directly from the chef's hands to yours so the nori stays shatteringly crisp. The Moso Omakase set runs you through hamachi, lobster, akami, toro, and eel, and the tastings, toro tartare, hamachi with ponzu and yuzu oil, show off aged fish at its best. Calm, minimalist, and quietly thrilling. Sit at the bar and order the set.

places.name: Nami
places.address: Nami, 6004 Artist Ave, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Lake Nona's Wave Hotel hides one of Orlando's transporting dining rooms. Nami, a Michelin-recommended contemporary Japanese restaurant, is built around drama done right: a backlit, undulating wooden ceiling, Japanese maple trees anchoring the room, and a sleek bar made for lingering. The menu goes bold and global, lobster donuts, BBQ eel donburi, A5 steak, refined small plates that keep surprising, and the separate Chef's Counter turns dinner into an extended chef-led tasting. Precision, artistry, and a cocktail program with tableside flair. Dress up and make it a night.

places.name: New General
places.address: New General, 155 E New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4330
places.description: Part café, part modern general store, entirely Winter Park charm. New General on New England Avenue is the health-forward hangout where clean ingredients meet genuinely great coffee: the blueberry lavender latte is the drink everyone tells their friends about, the matcha and cold brew are dialed in, and the Blue Majik latte brings a little theater to your cup. Shroom avo toast, acai bowls, frittatas, and gluten-friendly everything keep the food side fresh, and while you wait you can browse shelves of small-batch soaps, granolas, and goods. Plant-filled, bright, and quietly the feel-good room of the neighborhood.

places.name: Nile Ethiopian
places.address: Nile Ethiopian, 7048 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-8222
places.description: Family-run Nile has served traditional Ethiopian cuisine since 2006, quietly building a loyal following on International Drive. Everything arrives shared, mounded on spongy injera that you tear and scoop. The vegan Taste of the Nile brings shiro, lentils, and collard greens, while the Chef's Special adds doro wat, kitfo, and sizzling beef tibs. Regulars describe meals here among the best they have had in Orlando. The room feels warm and lovely, and a traditional coffee ceremony rewards patience. Pick it for a cultural evening on I-Drive.

places.name: Noir Bar
places.address: 861 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801 (inside Talay Thai)
places.description: First you find the Thai restaurant, then you find the door hidden inside it. Noir Bar sits behind Talay Thai downtown, dark and moody in the true speakeasy mold and made for date night. Craft cocktails lead, including a pandan and matcha blend that tastes as intriguing as it sounds, while Thai inspired bites keep pace with the drinks. Dine at Talay first, then slip through the wall and let the evening turn cinematic. Choose it when being in on the secret is half the pleasure.

places.name: Nomikai by Sushi Saint
places.address: 8371 International Dr Ste 60, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Chef Michael Collantes, behind Michelin-starred Soseki and Bib Gourmand Sushi Saint, just went big. Nomikai by Sushi Saint at ICON Park is his boldest concept yet, and the name says it all: the Japanese art of the celebratory gathering, food and drink and friends. Sushi Saint's greatest hits show up, salmon aguachile, hamachi truffle potato, a large-format omakase platter, joined by shareable showstoppers like dry-aged tomahawk and lobster noodles. The room is his "Tokyo neo-cyberpunk" vision, neon blues, original art, dark and moody with electronica. Local chefs planting a flag on I-Drive: this is how the tourist corridor grows up.

places.name: Norigami
places.address: Norigami, 426 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787-3014
places.description: A tiny counter and a streak of Michelin Bib Gourmands: Winter Garden's Norigami proves great things come in the smallest rooms. Chef David Tsan works with surgical precision inside Plant Street Market, where the name, nori plus origami, becomes a ritual: every piece of sushi arrives on colorful washi paper that guests fold into cranes for the growing centerpiece bowl. The omakase is the move, popcorn hamachi and toro carpaccio with truffle among the standouts, the rice seasoned and loosely packed just right. Polished, warm, and worth the trip west. Book ahead, the counter fills fast.

places.name: Oga's Cantina
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A droid DJ, a tingling cocktail, and a room built for Star Wars fans. Oga's Cantina sits inside Galaxy's Edge at Hollywood Studios, where R-3X spins behind the bar and drinks arrive in otherworldly presentations. The Fuzzy Tauntaun famously makes your mouth tingle, joined by Bespin Fizz, Outer Rim, and non alcoholic options for younger guests, plus galactic snacks. Space is tight, the energy is high, and reservations are hard to land. Book ahead if Batuu is on your park day plan.

places.name: Orlando International Airport (MCO)
places.address: 1 Jeff Fuqua Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: The trip starts or ends here, and lately it is eating well. Orlando International has quietly built a strong airport food scene, and it keeps getting more local: 4Rivers smokehouse barbecue, Black Bean Deli's Cuban sandwiches, Otto's High Dive cocktails, Maxine's on Shine from Thornton Park, Kelly's Homemade Ice Cream, Seito Sushi, and Smoke & Donuts bringing brisket and crullers together like nobody else. The iconic carpet is still the first photo, but your last taste of Orlando can now be genuinely delicious. Build in a buffer and eat here, not on the plane.

places.name: Orlando Science Center
places.address: 777 E Princeton St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Every Orlando kid of the last thirty years has a Science Center memory, and many involve that dome. The Orlando Science Center started in 1960 as the Central Florida Museum and grew into four floors of hands-on exhibits in Loch Haven Park: dinosaur digs, a living cypress swamp and the observatory roof. The Dome by Dr. Phillips Charities is the place's soul, a 300-seat giant dome theater that surrounds you with Everest climbs and ocean depths. Go learn something and feel like a kid again, whatever your age.

places.name: The Osprey
places.address: The Osprey, 4899 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6629
places.description: Baldwin Park's beloved dining room does a little of everything, and does it well. The Osprey, the Good Salt Group's New Broad Street anchor since 2015, pairs an open kitchen and a buzzing central bar with New American cooking with a seafood soul. Comfort classics like cottage pie and homemade bolognese share the menu with Florida fish, grilled oysters and a thoughtful oyster bar streak. The weekday happy hour oysters are local legend, desserts close things sweetly, and the chef's table rewards the truly committed. Book it for lively, comfortable service.

places.name: Osteria Ester
places.address: 629 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: The Good Salt crew keeps landing in the right rooms. Osteria Ester, from the team behind the Osprey and Seito Sushi, takes over the old Soco space on East Central and turns it into a love letter to chef-partner Michael Cooper's grandmother: classic Italian-American cooking in a warm, neighborhood setting. Fresh pasta, house-baked focaccia, and the kind of unpretentious hospitality that made the group's other rooms famous. This is the Italian joint you can live with: date nights, family tables, and that perfect post-work glass. Worth a look in Thornton Park to see what this team does next.

places.name: Otto's High Dive
places.address: 2304 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A grandfather who poured drinks in Manzanillo during Cuba's cocktail golden age gave Otto's its name and its compass. Co-owner Giovanni Fernandez's family story shapes this Milk District rum bar, which holds Bib Gourmand recognition. Ropa vieja and lechon asado sit beside Florida seafood and a serious raw bar, while daiquiris and house builds take the 1950s Havana canon seriously. Cafe Abundancia covers mornings and brunch covers weekends. Book ahead, because the dim, greenery lined room fills with date night energy.

places.name: Palm Beach Meats
places.address: Palm Beach Meats, 3421 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32806-6127
places.description: Wagyu, done every way, is the single obsession behind Palm Beach Meats on South Orange. Eric and Meghan San Pedro built the shop and restaurant around Japanese, Australian and American Wagyu. The counter serves a Wagyu burger, a layered Frito Pie, Filipino leaning Wagyu tapa over garlic rice with a fried egg, a Wagyu Philly and a beef tallow Nutella brownie people return for. Behind the coolers, a full market holds Wagyu deli cuts and frozen beef. Carnivores get a pilgrimage spot with fast casual ease out front.

places.name: Peach Valley Cafe
places.address: Peach Valley Cafe, 2849 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806-5403
places.description: Hot apple fritters arrive first, and patience gets tested immediately. Peach Valley has served Central Florida as a neighborhood brunch answer since 2001, a local chain that still cooks like a name is on the sign. Chicken and waffles come with blueberry butter and Cajun spiked syrup, and shrimp and grits taste of the low country. A sunlit porch suits slow mornings and big crews around the table. Choose it when everyone at your table needs a plate that feels made for them, from fritters to grits and back again.

places.name: Perla's Pizza, Vinyl Records & Cocktail Bar
places.address: 959 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A thin, crackling crust, playlists spun live on vinyl and a cocktail in your hand while the pies fly: Perla's runs on all three at once. Chef-driven and joyfully nontraditional, the room is curated by chef Mike Collantes. A banana-topped pie sits on the menu and somehow works; a tikka-spiced pie works even better, regulars say. Come for the slice, and stay because the spinning-record buzz of the room feels like a party that never tips over. It is Winter Park pizza with a record collection.

places.name: Permanent Vacation
places.address: Permanent Vacation, 106 Lake Ave, Maitland, FL 32751-6424
places.description: An Employees Only door inside a Maitland sports bar opens onto a different state of mind. Permanent Vacation is a tiki speakeasy hidden inside the Copper Rocket, committed to skulls and bamboo, fish floats in netting overhead, and fog rolling through the dark. Your bartender, billed as a travel agent, hands you a rum cocktail and a tab in a passport. The Pearl Necklace is the drink people talk about most. Reserve ahead, because regulars treat a return visit like checking in on old friends.

places.name: Pho Hoa
places.address: Pho Hoa, 649 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5016
places.description: On a side street off Colonial, Orlando goes to Pho Hoa when it wants Vietnamese food without the performance. A bright, family-style room is built around a broth that tastes like someone refused to cut a corner: deep, clear and alive with star anise. The pho bo is the order you see at half the tables, the bun bo hue brings a slow chili warmth, and the Vietnamese iced coffee is famously thick. Unfussy and generous, it is exactly the kind of Mills 50 place locals quietly depend on.

places.name: Pizza Bruno
places.address: Pizza Bruno, 3990 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-2702
places.description: Order the garlic knots first; the table will be glad you did. Pizza Bruno is owner Bruno Zacchini's love letter to the Jersey shore summers that taught him dough, turned into a wood-fired Neapolitan room on Curry Ford Road. The crust is naturally leavened, blistered and chewy, and the place hums with neighborhood conviction. Pies are playful but never gimmicky, built on tight technique, and a second location in College Park covers the craving west of the tracks. It is the Curry Ford pizza night regulars defend.

places.name: Prato
places.address: Prato, 124 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Right on Park Avenue, with window-paned doors thrown open to the brick street, Prato is Winter Park's idea of Italian and it is a good one. House-made pastas, wood-fired pies, and a long bar that practically begs you to linger. The mustard spaghettini cacio e pepe is the dish people drive across town for, peppery and silky in equal measure, and the pretzel-crusted calamari proves a pub snack can be elegant. A Michelin-selected room that never feels stiff, only sunlit, generous, and alive.

places.name: Raglan Road
places.address: 1640 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Mahogany and walnut salvaged from old Irish bars and churches give this room its weight. Raglan Road, Disney Springs' Dublin style pub, takes its name from the Kavanagh poem later turned into song by U2 and Van Morrison. Live bands and Irish dancers perform nightly, a weekend brunch show rolls on, fish and chips draw people across the property, and the whiskey list takes its job seriously. Choose it when you want a Disney Springs room that locals bring visitors to and then stay for themselves.

places.name: Ramen Takagi
places.address: Ramen Takagi, 3635 Aloma Ave, Oviedo, FL 32765-6395
places.description: Out in Oviedo, far from the ramen crowds, a small shop rewards the drive across the county. Ramen Takagi cooks everything from scratch in a space that feels like a kitchen that happens to serve the public. The black garlic tonkotsu is the signature, deep and savory with a roasted edge, the spicy miso brings real heat, and the tantan mazesoba proves the kitchen can do brothless too. Go at lunch, order warm, and plan to return for the whole menu. Serious noodle people already treat it as a destination.

places.name: Ravello
places.address: 10100 Dream Tree Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Some Italian dinners earn a plan made weeks ahead, birthday included. Ravello sits inside the Four Seasons Resort Orlando, where executive chef Fabrizio Schenardi, a Torino native, runs a kitchen that makes its pastas, breads, sauces, and desserts entirely in house. The veal ravioli is the signature, soft and rich the way holiday meals are remembered, and the wood-fired pies come layered with prosciutto di Parma and fresh burrata. It even holds a rare Italian taste certification few American restaurants ever earn. Bring someone you want to impress. The room will help.

places.name: Reyes Mezcaleria
places.address: Reyes Mezcaleria, 821 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1014
places.description: Chef Wendy Lopez, a Michoacán native, cooks the Mexico she grew up with in Downtown North. Reyes pours more than 150 agave spirits alongside her cooking, and the whole room hums with that kind of intention. The Good Salt Restaurant Group, the family behind some of Orlando's most loved dining rooms, founded Reyes in 2017 with one mission: honor the cuisine, the spirits and the culture of Mexico. Every plate feels rooted and every pour feels considered. Pick it when you want Mexican cooking with soul and a bar with real depth behind it.

places.name: Rion's Ocean Room
places.address: Rion's Ocean Room, 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Inside East End Market, a walk-up poke counter does one thing honestly. Rion's Ocean Room cuts fish fresh and treats it with respect: premium ahi, fatty salmon, ono, Hawaiian tobiko style, and inari bombs regulars talk about like folklore. Order over carefully cooked rice or buy by the pound when you mean business. No frills distract from glistening fish and clean flavor. Come to Winter Park's market counter when you want proof that Orlando can eat like it has an ocean, without dressing up the experience.

places.name: Salt & Cellar
places.address: Salt & the Cellar by Akira Back, 3001 Sherberth Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34747-1787
places.description: Low light does real work here, making an evening feel like an occasion early. Inside the Ette Hotel in Kissimmee, chef Akira Back's Salt & Cellar moves across steakhouse, Mediterranean, and Japanese-leaning Asian flavors. Table lamps, smart service, and a polished, dim room set the tone before courses land. Guests talk about the Sunday afternoon tea long after a visit. The kitchen carries the confidence of a chef who has cooked on big stages. Pick it for a date night south of Disney that delivers on its lighting.

places.name: Seby's Pizza
places.address: Seby's Pizza, 1555 Semoran Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792-1501
places.description: Chef Sebastian "Seby" Donofrio is a third-generation Italian-American making the New York pie he grew up on, in a tiny plaza where Casselberry fades into Winter Park. The menu reads like a love letter to Manhattan street names: the Soho, the Rubirosa and the Nolita, each a thin, foldable, hand-tossed slice with house-made dough and a scratch sauce that stays honest, never sweet. He uses reverse-osmosis water and never-frozen mozzarella. Opened in 2025 and already spoken of like an institution, with amaretto cream cake as the sleeper hit.

places.name: Seito Sushi
places.address: Seito Sushi, 4898 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814
places.description: On New Broad Street in Baldwin Park, Seito has spent more than two decades proving that sushi in Central Florida can be both traditional and fearlessly modern. Executive chef Huy Tin runs a kitchen that honors classic technique while inventing with it: tuna crispy rice with smoked trout roe, torch salmon, bluefin chutoro sashimi, and a six-course chef's tasting for the truly committed. The room is dim and elegant, the kind of place anniversaries default to. It is sushi as a quiet art form, and it has the staying power to prove it.

places.name: Selam Ethiopian
places.address: Selam, 5494 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-8774
places.description: Eating here is a ceremony you perform with your hands. Selam serves Ethiopian and Eritrean cooking on Central Florida Parkway, with wats and tibs on platters built for sharing over injera you tear and scoop. A traditional buna coffee ritual arrives fragrant from the roast, and staff walk first-timers through everything with genuine warmth. Tej, a honey wine, makes the right companion at the table. Order the combination platter and go with people you like. Surrender to the communal joy, and let the room treat you as an honored guest.

places.name: Selva Rosa
places.address: 901 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Mexican and Japanese cooking collide here, and the plates land like a party. Selva Rosa serves birria tempura sushi, hamachi in bright green sauces, short rib taquizas and a matcha mojito people photograph before tasting. Tuesday brings the tacos and sushi night that has Maitland buzzing, with all you can eat tacos in the mix. The room runs loud and colorful, full of plates that stop conversation. Pick it for fusion with imagination, not fusion as a gimmick.

places.name: Shin Jung
places.address: 1638 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Tabletop grills have been sizzling on this room's tables since 1993. Shin Jung, one of the first Korean restaurants in Orlando, survived a fire and returned rebuilt and brighter, with K-pop on the screens and the room humming. The banchan spread is generous, LA kalbi and beef bulgogi carry real flame character, and the soon tofu stew arrives bubbling. Go with a group, order for the table, and let dinner become an event built around sharing, grilling, and passing plates.

places.name: Shiraz Market
places.address: 188 S US Hwy 17-92, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Half Persian grocery, half sizzling grill counter, Shiraz Market turns a spice run into lunch. The Longwood shop holds a hot food case with tender chicken koobideh, beef kebabs and falafel, plus hummus, baba ganoush and other mezze made with halal ingredients. Browse shelves of Persian sweets and teas while your food hits the grill, then eat at the counter like a regular. The detour up 17-92 pays off in kebabs. Come for ingredients and leave with a platter you did not plan on.

places.name: Six Ravens
places.address: 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Savory was the missing move from the people behind Gideon's Bakehouse, and Disney Springs feels it. Six Ravens, in The Landing, serves Coffyns, old school hand pies made from house baked yeast rolls with chef driven fillings. The menu reads like a love letter to Orlando food: a Pizza Bruno collaboration with basil pesto chicken, a Smoke and Donuts mashup of pulled pork and mac and cheese, and a Pink Salamander cheeseburger pie. Local draft beer from Sideward Brewing and The Ravenous Pig rounds it out. Choose Six Ravens for a dark, storybook grab and go between adventures.

places.name: Smoke & Donuts BBQ
places.address: 601 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Brisket and cake donuts sound like a dare until the Lou Donut lands on your table. Chef Ian Russell, a Culinary Institute of America graduate, fell for roadside smoke on a cross country trip before opening this family run Milk District spot. Low and slow USDA Prime brisket, Carolina pulled pork, and brown butter turkey share the menu with made to order donuts. The Lou carries bourbon maple glaze, chocolate, and brisket burnt ends, while classic rock keeps the room loud.

places.name: Smokemade Meats + Eats
places.address: 1400 S Crystal Lake Dr, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Concrete floors, a menu on butcher paper, and brisket doing the talking. Pitmaster Tyler Brunache learned Central Texas barbecue running pop-ups in DC that sold out in minutes, then came home to Orlando and opened Smokemade on Curry Ford West. Salt and pepper pork ribs carry a proper smoky edge, jalapeno cheddar sausage holds its own beside Texas benchmarks, and house baked bread comes alongside everything. Come hungry, greet the pitmaster if you get the chance, and expect to plan a return visit.

places.name: Sodough Square
places.address: Sodough Square, 419 E Michigan St, Orlando, FL 32806-4511
places.description: A Detroit native built a square slice on Michigan Street, and the pan does the talking. SoDough Square serves Detroit-style pizza with a caramelized cheese edge crackling down the corners of every pan, the way owner Robert Bair remembers it from the Motor City. The menu leans playful: the Detroit Rob City with hot honey, a taco pizza, and a Big Mac tribute. Dough sometimes sells out, and a Winter Park location has followed. Order early, and get the cheesy garlic bread alongside.

places.name: Sorekara
places.address: Sorekara, 4979 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6414
places.description: Orlando's first two-Michelin-star restaurant hides on a Baldwin Park street, and dining there is closer to theater than dinner. Chef William Shen built Sorekara around Japan's 72 micro seasons, so the 20-plus course tasting menu reinvents itself every week or so, moving guests through multiple rooms over several hours. There is deep refinement here: Hokkaido crab, madai with a sly twist, desserts that close the night like a finale. And there is mischief too, a course that plays with a convenience-store snack run. One seating a night, a few nights a week, and worth every bit of planning it takes.

places.name: Soseki Modern Omakase
places.address: 955 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Ten seats, one chef's counter, and a Michelin star earned within a year of opening. Soseki is chef Michael Collantes' intimate omakase room on Fairbanks Avenue, where fish from Japan meets the bounty of Central Florida on plates made by Florida artisans. Every piece of nigiri lands with precision and a story, and the tea pairing has its own following among those who skip the sake. This is dinner as a private performance, personal, playful, and precise. Book the moment you know you are going. Seats this small never wait around.

faqs.a: Book at sosekifl.com - tickets are nonrefundable, about $259 per person. Reserve far ahead; the 10-seat counter sells out.

places.name: Sparrow Orlando
places.address: 807 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: You settle into a dark, moody room in Mills 50 and the night slows down on purpose. Sparrow is the wine bar and lounge from the Good Salt group, with chef Wendy Lopez cooking southern European small plates. You can order silky mushroom pate, jamon iberico with melon, short rib ragu over rigatoni, and a tomato gimlet that wakes up your palate. The wine list leans Old World with New World charm, and Thursday vinyl nights give the room its pulse. Choose Sparrow for an intimate, unhurried date night that feels grown up and a little romantic.

places.name: Stasio's Italian Deli
places.address: 2320 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: On the corner of Bumby and Robinson sits the kind of Italian deli that turns lunch into a small celebration. Stasio's piles its signature sandwich high with prosciutto, hot capicola, soppressata, and fresh mozzarella on house-baked bread, and the chicken parm sub has its own devoted following. Come for a morning sfogliatelle filled with orange-scented ricotta and a proper espresso, then browse the market shelves for imported pastas and pantry goods on the way out. Regulars and first-timers get the same warm bustle. This is the Milk District's little Italy, and it earns every bit of its love.

places.name: Still Lounge by Dre and Snoop
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Dre and Snoop put their names on a room, and the room behaves like it knows. Inside Live! at Pointe Orlando, this second lounge from Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg pairs dark wood and leather couches with golden light. DJs and live performers rotate through hip hop, R and B, and soul while the bar centers on the duo's Still G.I.N. You can sip a Platinum Negroni, a lavender honey Bee's Knees, or the bourbon based OG-OF. Choose it for an upscale night that stays loose, curated, and built for lingering after dark.

places.name: Sushi Saint
places.address: 400 Pittman St Ste A, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: From Michelin-starred chef Michael Collantes, the mind behind Soseki, comes the fun sibling: a temaki handroll bar where chefs build cone-shaped handrolls right in front of you. The original Creative Village room earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its obsessive sourcing, tuna with scallion and wasabi, snow crab with truffle and finger lime, A5 wagyu with truffle mushroom jam. There is a lounge for cocktails, a 12-seat omakase for the devoted, and a newer Icon Park outpost for the I-Drive crowd. It is high-end sushi served with lounge energy, and it never takes itself too seriously.

places.name: Taverna Opa
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Dinner becomes a party you joined on purpose at this International Drive Greek taverna. Taverna Opa starts classic with whitewashed walls, saganaki flaming tableside, wood fired lamb chops, fresh Mediterranean seafood and a mezze spread for the whole table. Then a belly dancer appears, the Zorba line dance pulls you in and napkins rain as confetti. Later, a live DJ deepens the celebration. Bring your loudest friends, or plan to become one before the plates are cleared.

places.name: Thai House
places.address: Thai House, 2117 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4834
places.description: Look for the red building with the green roof on East Colonial. Inside is Thai House of Orlando, a Mills 50 fixture that keeps its cooking close to the Thai original. The room is small and cozy, the kind of place where regulars barely glance at the menu. The pad panang is rich and comforting, the duck soup has a loyal following, and the curries carry real depth. Locals have defended this place for years against every newcomer. End with the fried banana and ice cream, and you will understand the loyalty.

places.name: The Beacham & The Social
places.address: 46 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A century-old vaudeville theater on Orange Avenue still does what it has done since 1921: give Orlando a place to lose itself in music. The Beacham went from vaudeville acts to a movie house to the city's defining concert hall and nightclub, and its stage has hosted Devo, The Police, Soundgarden, Pink and Lauryn Hill. National tours fill the floor, and late on weekends it turns into a full nightclub. There is history in these walls and bass in the floorboards. Stand up front once; it spoils lesser rooms.

places.name: The Boathouse & Vintage Amphicars
places.address: 1620 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Waterfront dining is easy to promise at Disney Springs; owning the view is harder. The Boathouse pairs a raw bar and steaks, both with reputations earned honestly, with a deck where golden hour slows the table down. Then comes the signature move: a captain-guided Amphicar tour in a vintage 1960s amphibious car that splashes off the dock and carries you around the lake. The house bills it as a singular experience worldwide. Book the ride, then dinner, when you want the evening to feel staged around water.

places.name: The Glass Knife
places.address: The Glass Knife, 276 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Antique glass cake knives on the wall explain the name before the menu does. The Glass Knife is a French cafe that grew up in Florida, opened in Winter Park with intention in every detail. Its creme brulee donut, made from 24 hour buttermilk brioche, has a following of its own, and the coffee is Onyx, pulled fresh each time. Weekend brunch brings full table service, while weekdays run counter order with lingering on the covered patio encouraged. Choose it for a slower, polished morning.

places.name: The Majesty Building ("The I-4 Eyesore")
places.address: 123 E Central Pkwy, Altamonte Springs, FL 32701
places.description: Every Orlando commuter knows the half-finished tower looming over I-4 in Altamonte Springs. Construction on the 18-story Majesty Building has been underway since 2001 and somehow never finished. It is the pet project of religious broadcaster Claud Bowers of SuperChannel 55, built donation by donation, debt-free, at a pace that made it a local legend and the punchline of a thousand commute jokes. Gawk at it on your drive and ask any local about it. Few landmarks tell you as much about Central Florida's patience and humor.

places.name: The Moderne
places.address: 1241 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Art Deco curves and tableside smoke give Mills 50 its most theatrical cocktail room. The Moderne pairs gold accents and sculptural lines with chef owner Michael Nguyen's bar program built around deconstructed classics: smoked old fashioneds poured tableside, elaborate garnishes, and drinks such as Woman in White. Plates follow the same logic, ranging tapas style from Korean vodka pasta to duck wontons and miso cream noodles, drawing on the district's heritage. Book it when a date night should feel like an occasion with ceremony built in.

places.name: The Monroe
places.address: The Monroe, 448 N Terry Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1894
places.description: Childhood favorites grow up in an airy midcentury room at The Monroe. The Good Salt group's fourth concept sits on the ground floor of the Julian apartments in Creative Village, built as a diverse social gathering place. You get famous fried chicken, pork belly s'mores, and jalapeno popper deviled eggs, plus a coffee bar by day that turns cocktail bar by night. Next door, the Front Porch overlooks Luminary Green Park. Choose it for a working lunch, a long happy hour, or a dinner that lingers without any effort from you.

places.name: The Pinery
places.address: The Pinery, 295 NE Ivanhoe Blvd, Orlando, FL 32804-6434
places.description: Right on Lake Ivanhoe, The Pinery is Ivanhoe Village's love letter to its own past, named for the pineapple farms that once grew where the condos stand. Owner Carol Holladay runs a warm, lake-view dining room built on Southern hospitality and chef-driven Florida cooking: smoked peanut soup, a bread board with pimento cheese, broiled blue crab dip, and shrimp and grits that taste like the season they were made in. The patio catches the water breeze, the cocktails lean tropical, and the whole room glows. Dinner with a view, done the Ivanhoe way.

places.name: The Ravenous Pig & Brewing Co.
places.address: 565 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Ask a Winter Park local where to eat and watch their face change when they say this name. Husband-and-wife chefs James and Julie Petrakis turned a warm, butcher-shop-beautiful gastropub into the restaurant that taught Orlando to take its own food seriously.
