The kitchen is run by two Top Chef alums who refuse to serve ordinary bar food, so you eat better than the usual sports bar standard. Drinks stay in hand, nobody sits still, and the roar moves through fans around you. Pick Stadium Club when you want a watch party with scale, energy, and food that keeps pace.

places.name: Duffy's Sports Grill
places.address: Duffy's Sports Grill, 951 Market Promenade Ave, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Screens everywhere and the game always on: Duffy's knows its assignment in Lake Mary. The Florida sports bar chain built its name on taking game day seriously, and this location adds a big, busy patio that stays active through the season. The Major League Burger and jumbo wings headline a kitchen that treats game day food with real care. Bring the crew, find your screen early, and settle in for the kind of loud, happy room where nobody watches a big play alone.

places.name: Krungthep Tea Time
places.address: 1051 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Krungthep is the Thai name for Bangkok, and this Winter Park tea room carries that city into every cup. The Gra-prow chicken sandwich lands sweet, spicy, and savory at once, while Thai iced tea earns the kind of praise people write love notes about. Brick toast desserts arrive dressed in condensed milk, coconut ice cream, and matcha for a slower finish. The black and white room feels calm and design forward, built for long chats over loose leaf tea. Choose Krungthep when an afternoon calls for tea, spice, and dessert in equal measure.

places.name: Maitland Chocolate Factory
places.address: 445 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: A working chocolate shop beats a gift store that happens to sell candy. Maitland Chocolate Factory makes handmade truffles, dipped strawberries, and fudge in the back each morning, then fills the front case with them. Roughly a thousand themed molds let the shop turn chocolate into almost anything for a birthday, wedding, or ordinary Tuesday. The Dubai chocolate bar is the current craze, but classics keep Maitland returning. Come when you want chocolate made on site, shaped imaginatively, and grounded in everyday local habit.

places.name: Metro Diner (Kissimmee)
places.address: 2714 Osceola Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: A great diner does comfort food without irony, and Metro Diner has practiced since Jacksonville in 1992. Now a Florida institution, the Kissimmee room serves fried chicken and waffles, cinnamon roll pancakes that draw weekend lines, and biscuits with sausage gravy exactly as they should arrive. All day breakfast, hearty sandwiches, and fried chicken done right fill out the menu, all served with genuine warmth. Bring visitors here when you want to show them what a diner is supposed to be, without dressing the idea up at all.

places.name: Puro Dulzor by Karolene
places.address: 1354 E Vine St, Kissimmee, FL 34744
places.description: Pure sweetness is the name translated, and the Kissimmee kitchen earns it starting with the coffee. People rave about the coffee first, then you stay for Puerto Rican breakfast: a towering Tripleta sandwich, crisp empanadillas, and crema de maiz like abuela made it. A mayorca stuffed with Nutella gives you the sweet finish. The room feels like a cozy island kitchen, and the team treats you like family from the first visit. Choose Puro Dulzor when you want warmth, coffee, and breakfast with a Puerto Rican heartbeat.

places.name: Cocina Maya Mexican Grill & Mezcaleria
places.address: 3590 US-17 Ste 1026, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Charred chili and warm corn perfume this Lake Mary kitchen, where Mexican cooking is treated as an art form. Cocina Maya serves Holy Guacamole, Mayan tortilla soup that tastes like a guarded family recipe, salmon in mezcal sauce and camarones a la diabla that go far beyond taco shop basics. A mezcal cocktail puts smoke in the glass to match the fire on the plate. Order one and slow down. The menu rewards diners who came for more than the familiar standards.

places.name: Hooked Fish Camp
places.address: 550 Towne Center Cir, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: The F&D crew brought a fish camp concept to Sanford, and the room keeps that promise. Hooked Fish Camp offers rustic cabin warmth and seafood done the relaxed Florida way. Start with clam chowder, a pile of mussels, and hush puppies, then stay for crab legs and a slab of lemon pie sized for the whole table. The operation feels new, friendly, and clear about exactly what it is. Pick it when you want Sanford seafood without formality, especially with a table that shares starters and dessert.

places.name: Green Papaya Thai & Sushi
places.address: 2480 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32779
places.description: One kitchen, two traditions, no compromise promised or needed. Green Papaya runs a Thai menu and a full sushi bar side by side, and both sides earn their keep: the Tom Kha soup is the kind you talk about afterward, the pad thai and drunken noodles hit every note, and the duck with yellow curry could carry a restaurant on its own. The sushi rolls are fresh, the room is polished and modern, and the format works just as well for a date as for dinner with the whole crew.

places.name: Southern Steer Butcher (Orlando)
places.address: 11024 W Colonial Dr, Ocoee, FL 34761
places.description: Grocery store meat counters have a higher standard to meet in Ocoee. Southern Steer is family owned, serious about guest service and focused on sourcing, with all natural, humanely processed meat now dry aged in house. Staff walk you through the case, teach you how to cook what you buy and may talk you into the armadillo eggs. Part butcher, part neighborhood food school, it rewards the drive out Colonial. Go when you want advice with the cut, not just a package.

places.name: The Twisted Chopstick
places.address: 412 S Woodland Blvd, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: Woodland Boulevard in DeLand has a sushi stop built around family ownership and a playful Godzilla spirit. Set in a historic building, the room keeps things approachable while the kitchen sends out Fire Tonkatsu Ramen with real heat. The Black Widow and Samurai rolls lead the sushi side, and poke bowls plus sushi burritos widen the order for mixed tastes. You get creativity without formality, which makes it an easy recommendation for a relaxed DeLand dinner with friends.

places.name: Crooked Can Minneola
places.address: 1600 Crooked Can Loop, Minneola, FL 34715
places.description: Winter Garden's beloved brewery went big in Minneola, and the scale changes the outing. The City Center complex packs a full production brewery and canning line, a sprawling taproom, and a food hall of 11 local vendors chosen to spotlight Lake County flavor. Out back, a beer garden, a live music stage, and a splash pad give groups room to spread out. Core brews and seasonal one offs pour at the new Crooked Can headquarters. Choose it when you want a destination brewery built as Minneola's gathering place, not just a taproom stop.

places.name: BTW Burgers Tacos Waffles
places.address: 115 E Main St, Tavares, FL 32778
places.description: Tavares punches above its weight when one counter handles burgers, tacos, and waffles with imagination. BTW does exactly what the name promises and gives each lane real attention. Winner Winner chicken and waffles uses crispy, never over breaded chicken, the Black N Blue burger gets called unbelievable by people who order it, and tacos bring real kick. The waffle menu adds a caramel rum Half Witted Monkey and deep fried Oreos. Set beside Brü Tap House, it lets your beer and burger meet in the middle of the room.

places.name: Harrell's Hot Dogs and Cold Cones
places.address: 54 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Plant Street stays busy, and Harrell's keeps the hot dog sacred through the rush. All beef dogs are grilled, never boiled, so every bite carries char. You can build your own from a wall of toppings or order a signature like the Chicago Dog or the Mac Monster. Fresh cut fries arrive seasoned and crisp, and a cold cone finishes the meal the right way. Grab a seat outside and watch Plant Street stroll by as Winter Garden moves around you. Choose Harrell's when a classic dog, crisp fries, and people watching beat a complicated lunch plan.

places.name: PokeWorks (Oviedo)
places.address: 45 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: Poke done right is fast, fresh, and exactly the way you want it, and PokeWorks in Oviedo nails the formula. Build your own bowl from sushi-grade ahi tuna, salmon, albacore, shrimp, and scallops over rice or greens, or go straight to the signatures: the Hawaiian Ahi, the yuzu ponzu salmon, the umami ahi. There are poke burritos, bite-size poke bombs, and the garlic spam musubi that regulars order on the side. Healthy never felt this satisfying.

places.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
places.address: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, Space Commerce Way, Merritt Island, FL 32953
places.description: There is nothing on this earth quite like standing beneath a real spaceship. At the Visitor Complex you walk the ground where America went to the Moon, come face to face with the Space Shuttle Atlantis, and ride the bus tour out to the Apollo/Saturn V Center, where a Saturn V hangs overhead like the future it still promises. Meet a veteran astronaut, let the Rocket Garden remind you how small your worries are, and watch your kids decide, right there, to become astronauts.

places.name: Ivanhoe Park Brewing Company
places.address: 1300 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Local history pours into the pint here, starting with the name itself. Ivanhoe Park honors Lake Ivanhoe founder George Russell and the old Joyland amusement park that once stood nearby. The beer follows with personality, from crisp Park Hopp'r pilsner to bold Tupac ShaPorter. A reclaimed wood taproom and dog friendly beer garden hum with neighborhood energy, and rotating taps keep locals returning to see what is new. Choose this independent brewery when you want an Ivanhoe Village hangout where story, setting, and beer all pull together.

places.name: La Revancha Cuban Cafe
places.address: 7339 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: Pressing Cubans since 1998 gives a cafe a standard to defend, and La Revancha defends it. The East Colonial spot points to its pressed bread, roast pork and mustard as proof behind its own best in town claim. Order the ropa vieja platter for the full table version or the pan con bistec as the sleeper hit. A cortadito hits hard, guava pastries finish sweet, and service stays fast and unpretentious. You get exactly what a Cuban cafe should deliver, without decoration getting in the way.

places.name: Viet-Nomz
places.address: 11798 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Orlando's first fast-casual Vietnamese spot started with three friends who wanted great pho on the go, and it became a local chain. The King Pho bowl is built for serious appetites, the NOMZ-ster bowl packs grilled meats and garden vegetables, and the street fare keeps things playful: banh mi, bao, Nuoc-Nom wings and Wa-Pho fries. A fresh herb bar lets you finish your own bowl, and the Vietnamese coffee, including the matcha version, is dangerously good. It is the easy east-side answer when pho cannot wait.

places.name: Omelet Bar
places.address: 12250 Strategy Blvd Ste 401, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Morning becomes an event near UCF when the omelet itself is built to order. Omelet Bar lets you build from a fresh bar of fillings or go bold with signatures. The Bostonian stuffs lobster inside and finishes with lobster bisque, while the carne frittata pairs smoked brisket with sausage gravy. Bread bowls, benedicts, a chicken and waffle flight, and beignets round out a menu built to convert first timers. Choose it when you want brunch with range, from a custom omelet to a flight worth sharing with the table.

places.name: Market On South
places.address: 2603 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Fully plant based food wins over skeptics at this South Eola food hall. Market on South covers the cravings with Kind Cleaver's sandwiches, the OrangeBird sloppy joe, creamy baked mac and cheese and BBQ jackfruit with real smoke. Dessert is not an afterthought: the cookie monster cone and Cuban cafecito scoop make the ice cream counter a destination on its own. Skeptics enter and converts leave, usually after the jackfruit. Bring a hungry friend who doubts plant based cooking and let the menu argue.

places.name: At The Diner
places.address: 5072 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Breakfast arrives with a wink, then the stacks prove the kitchen is serious. At The Diner, pancakes lead the menu in cinnamon roll, Boston cream, and Fruity Pebbles versions, with new names still landing. The Bennyffle puts eggs benedict on a waffle, and chicken and waffles are done right beside it. The Dr Phillips location stays bright and warm, beloved by locals who know the group well. Choose it when you want a playful breakfast that still delivers the diner basics you came for, stack after stack.

places.name: Insomnia Cookies
places.address: 12101 University Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Warm cookies at your door solve a very specific UCF craving. Insomnia Cookies leans on delivery and gooey classics straight from the oven: chocolate chunk, double chocolate, and a salted caramel deluxe. The Cookiewich, two cookies pressed around ice cream, is the bold order, and vegan options widen the table. Nothing here pretends to be more than comfort delivered warm, which is precisely why it works near campus. Order it when the night needs dessert without a plan, a drive, or dishes afterward.

places.name: Shake Shack I-Drive
places.address: 8359 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A spin on the Orlando Eye earns a burger with sauce people recognize on sight. The I-Drive Shack serves the ShackBurger with its famous sauce, the SmokeShack piled with bacon and cherry peppers, and the fried portobello Shroom burger for vegetarians. Crinkle cut fries stay crisp to the last one, and hand spun shakes and frozen custard concretes close the deal, including the location only Orlandough. Dogs are welcome on the patio with biscuits of their own. Choose this Shack when theme park energy needs a fast, familiar, patio friendly reset.

places.name: The Polite Pig
places.address: 1536 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Quick service at Disney Springs rarely slows anyone down, but the smoke here earns a pause. The Polite Pig is a family run modern BBQ spot serving tender pork shoulder, coffee rubbed brisket, and St. Louis ribs. Fried chicken with hot honey and sweet potato tots that everyone steals from your tray round out the order, and a deep bourbon list pours from the tap. Finish with buttermilk chess pie, and choose this when theme park food needs to feel polished and genuinely fun.

places.name: Kai Asian Street Fare
places.address: 1555 State Rd 436 Ste 1171, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Two brothers from different mothers built Kai on a simple idea: strong Asian street food, all under one roof. The Korean fried wings are the headline, shattering-crisp and glossed in sauces from mango habanero to spicy garlic parmesan. The 24-hour tonkotsu ramen anchors the noodle side, the garlic noodles have their own following, and the sweet potato mochi donut is the sleeper dessert. Street-food range is the point here, so order across the menu and share everything. It suits groups who like to graze widely.

places.name: Main Street Pizza
places.address: 16 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: Downtown Kissimmee's answer to New York-style pizza does not hold back. The slices are famously bigger than your face, the handcrafted pies use fresh ingredients and old-school recipes, and the menu has real personality: the Buffalo Chicken with its white base, and the Colorado, which piles pepperoni, bacon, chicken tenders, mozzarella sticks and fries onto one pie. Do not skip the nitrogen ice cream for dessert. For a neighborhood pizza joint with one genuinely over-the-top signature pie, Main Street delivers the full performance.

places.name: Paloma Coffee Co.
places.address: 507 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: On Main Street in Windermere, Paloma is the kind of coffee shop that turns strangers into regulars. The lattes come strong, smooth, and never bitter, finished with a perfect leaf; the chai and house-baked croissants hold their own beside them. Seasonal specials like the Lucky Latte and the rose latte keep things playful. Black-and-white decor, plants everywhere, soft music, and a sidewalk seat when the weather is kind. Worth the short trip out of Orlando.

places.name: Dough Boyz Pizza
places.address: 201 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Oviedo found its New York slice at Dough Boyz, a family-owned spot with the swagger of a Brooklyn joint. Their line is famous locally: it is not the water, it is the recipe, and the Grandma Margherita, Brooklyn Sicilian and vodka margherita pies back it up. The chicken parm stuffed garlic knot is a cult object all its own, and the wings, baked then fried, come out tender. Big personality and bigger slices define the room. Central Florida clearly approves, and one Grandma pie explains the confidence.

places.name: Le Macaron Celebration
places.address: 671 Front St #110, Celebration, FL 34747
places.description: A small piece of Paris sits on the lakeside promenade in Celebration. Le Macaron lines its case with French macarons in more than twenty flavors, including salted caramel, pistachio, rose, Colombian coffee, and birthday cake, each crisp shelled and chewy at the center. Beyond macarons, you find buttery croissants, eclairs, beignets, house made gelato, and a proper espresso menu. Pause here when a Celebration stroll needs a sweet break, and let a coffee and two macarons reset the pace of your day.

places.name: Kobe Japanese Steakhouse
places.address: 8148 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Dinner and a show, Japanese-style. Kobé is family-owned and has been doing teppanyaki with flair across Central Florida for years: onion volcanoes, flying shrimp, chefs who turn a flat-top grill into a stage. The sirloin and seafood trio get the full treatment, the sushi side earns its keep with rolls like the Krabby Shrimp, and the soup dumplings are a sleeper pick. Lively, generous, and perfect for birthdays, date nights, or any night that deserves theater.

places.name: Twistee Treat
places.address: Twistee Treat, 4500 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32812
places.description: A 25-foot ice cream cone rising off International Drive is impossible to miss. Twistee Treat, a Florida landmark since 1983, serves real fresh soft serve the old-school way inside that giant cone. Creamy twists come in cups, cones, shakes, malts, and floats, plus the signature Brownie Boat and banana boat. A waffle taco and cookiewich keep kids happy after park days. Prices stay cheerful and the format stays simple. Choose it for a full stop of nostalgia, especially when soft serve should taste uncomplicated.

places.name: Jeremiah's Italian Ice
places.address: 877 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL
places.description: Born in Orlando in 1996, Jeremiah's turned Italian ice into a Florida rite of summer. The Gelati layers Italian ice with creamy soft-serve in more than forty flavors, from mango and cotton candy to sea salted caramel and the famous Scoop Froggy Frog. Shops stay bright, lines move fast, and the J-List rewards regulars who return through the heat. The format is simple, cold, and built for repeat visits. Choose a Gelati when you want Orlando-born dessert that cools you down without slowing the day.

places.name: Lake Nona Deli and Market
places.address: 8510 Insular Ln, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Village Walk gets a neighborhood heartbeat from a counter that refuses to be only one thing. Lake Nona Deli and Market combines deli, pizzeria, and market, built on Boar's Head meats and cheeses, Olde Hearth bread, and local farm fresh goods. The Italian Classic sandwich stacks thick, pizzas draw a loyal crowd, and market shelves cover everyday needs. Gelato and boutique wine events add reasons to linger beyond the sandwich run. Choose it when you want a third place where lunch, groceries, and community warmth share one address.

places.name: High Tide Harry's
places.address: 4645 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Family-owned and proudly local since 1995, this is the seafood joint airport-corridor locals swear by. High Tide Harry's piles on crab legs, lobster, charbroiled oysters, Dungeness crab, and the famous Captain's Seafood Combo. Blue Stew has its own devoted following, fishbowls come big, and nautical decor makes no apology. The room runs on easygoing, everybody-knows-your-name energy. Come for Orlando seafood the way locals eat it: generous, fun, and fresh, with enough shellfish variety to turn one order into a table project.

places.name: Margaritaville (CityWalk)
places.address: 6000 Universal Studios Plaza Ste 704, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: CityWalk does escapism in a margarita glass, with a volcano doing the centerpiece pour. Margaritaville, Jimmy Buffett's tropical escape at Universal CityWalk, pairs the open air Porch of Indecision with a giant ship's mast rising from the dining room and live bands at night. The Cheeseburger in Paradise and coconut shrimp keep the beach theme on the plate. Come for lunch, stay toward sunset and leave wearing a lei. You go for the scene first and the familiar songs of the room second.

places.name: Five Guys (CityWalk)
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A theme park burger stop gets serious when the counter is built for custom stacks. Five Guys landed on CityWalk's upper level with a breakfast sandwich built for the morning trek into the parks, before the menu settles into familiar classics. You stack burgers your way, hand cut fries arrive in an overflowing cup, and milkshakes stay thick enough to matter. After a full day on your feet, the red and white counter feels like a promise kept. Choose it when familiarity, volume, and a morning option matter more to you than novelty.

places.name: El Paraíso Del Marisco
places.address: 8421 S Orange Blossom Trl Ste 156, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Ecuador and Peru set the standard for this Orlando seafood kitchen. El Paraíso Del Marisco serves encebollado the way Manabí cooks it, ceviche mixto with bright Ecuadorian snap, and chaulafán de mariscos built to share. Bolón de verde and empanadas de verde serve the plantain devotees at the table. Everything arrives cooked to order, so the kitchen takes its time and the plate repays it. The room feels warm and unfussy, family-run in spirit, with soccer on screens. Regulars drive an hour and return weekly, which says plenty.

places.name: Topgolf Orlando
places.address: 9295 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Golf skill is optional here, and that is exactly the point. Across three floors and 102 climate controlled bays, micro chipped balls trace your shots toward glowing targets while the kitchen sends out burgers and a full bar keeps the table supplied. A rooftop terrace with fire pits draws the golden hour crowd, and games range from precision challenges to Angry Birds target play. Choose it for birthdays, conventions, and friendly rivalries when cosmic bowling energy sounds better than a quiet round.

places.name: World Food Trucks
places.address: 5811 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: A parking lot in Kissimmee works like a passport you can eat your way through. More than a hundred food trucks from more than twenty countries line the park, putting Latin American spice beside Asian flavors and Caribbean comfort beside street food you had not craved yet. Live entertainment keeps families and night owls circling, parking is free and the lot hums late into the night. The atmosphere feels like a block party with a world map. Come hungry and leave with a list for next time.

places.name: AJ's Press
places.address: 182 W State Rd 434 #1008, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: A pressed sandwich becomes a mission at this family owned Longwood counter. Every sandwich meets a locally baked bolillo or telera before the press crisps combinations with a Latin heartbeat. You can order mojo pork dripping with garlic mojo oil, a Cuban with Cantimpalo chorizo beside slow roasted pork, or beer braised brisket with cilantro sour cream. Breakfast serves all day, lattice chips are house made, and the owners remember you. Choose AJ's Press when you want a small shop with big devotion pressed into every bite.

places.name: Shake Shack Winter Park
places.address: 119 N Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The same ShackBurger tastes different when the patio looks over a lake. Winter Park's Shake Shack sits on Lake Killarney, and the back patio turns a fast casual run into a small occasion. You get crinkle cut cheese fries, a hand spun strawberry shake, and a burger that arrives pink and honest. Come at golden hour, claim an outside table, and let the lake handle the atmosphere while the fries stay hot. Choose it when you want the familiar Shack order slowed down by water, light, and a view you cannot get elsewhere.

places.name: Blaze Pizza
places.address: 4100 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: Pizza by the assembly line, done right. You walk the line pointing at more than thirty toppings, the dough is made from scratch, and a blazing hot oven turns your build into a crisp, leopard-spotted pie in minutes. Vegans, keto loyalists and picky kids all walk out with exactly the pizza they pictured, which is the whole design. Fast food with a pizzaiolo's conscience sounds like a contradiction, but the crust crackle is the proof. Blaze suits a group whose members refuse to share one topping list.

places.name: Rome's Flavours
places.address: Rome's Flavours, 124 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789-3819
places.description: A Roman family kitchen tucked onto Winter Park's Park Avenue, and the authenticity is not marketing: the owners are from Rome, the pasta is handmade, the Roman Holiday poster on the wall is practically a credential. The carbonara steals the show, the fettuccine Alfredo wins converts, meatballs get called the best in town, and pistachio cannolis close the deal. Sidewalk seating, a rotating wine list, and the quiet confidence of people who simply follow the Italian traditions.

places.name: Cuban American Cafe
places.address: 135 W Central Blvd Ste 160, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Inside a Downtown credit union, a family operated cafe presses a Cuban sandwich worth seeking out. Bread is baked fresh every morning and everything is made to order, from the pressed Cuban on real Cuban bread to a tripleta with real weight and bistec de palomilla for comfort seekers. Regulars call the coffee the best in town, and the cortadito backs the claim with every small cup. Come for lunch and leave with a guava pastry for the walk back.

places.name: LaSpada's Original Cheesesteaks and Hoagies
places.address: 1010 Lee Rd, Orlando, FL 32810
places.description: Delco standards arrive pre installed when the owner grew up with them. LaSpada's runs on family tradition and made to order pride, starting with a 12 inch original stacked with steak, sweet onions, and white American cheese. A mushroom cheesesteak draws people across counties, and the Famous Italian hoagie covers the table when beef is not the move. Guests talk about cheese distributed through every bite, a mountain of meat, and the sweetness of those onions. Choose LaSpada's for Philly in Orlando, with no translation needed at the counter.

places.name: Lombardi's Seafood
places.address: 1888 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Three generations of the Lombardi family have kept this Fairbanks Avenue market as the fish counter Orlando trusts, since the early fifties. Cases run deep: stone crab claws in season, whole snappers on ice, first-of-season Copper River sockeye when Alaska boats come through, and live crawfish when available. The little café cooks what the market sells, and bisque and fish tacos carry just-off-the-dock confidence. Chefs shop here, which tells home cooks where to start. Buy dinner, then let the café prove the case.

places.name: Peterbrooke Chocolatier
places.address: 300 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Park Avenue's chocolate shop has handcrafted in the European tradition since 1983, and you taste the discipline. Peterbrooke's signature chocolate-covered popcorn delivers a sweet-and-salty combination that can ruin ordinary snacks for you. Chocolate-dipped strawberries, truffles, handmade pretzels, and house gelato cover cases where chocolate alone is not enough. The locally owned shop smells of cocoa from the sidewalk and runs chocolate-making date nights where you build edible creations. Bring a gift budget with limits, because Winter Park chocolate makes restraint genuinely difficult here.

places.name: Cold Stone Creamery
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Dessert becomes theater on a frozen granite slab at CityWalk. Cold Stone crew members fold mix-ins into fresh-churned ice cream in front of you, sometimes singing while they work. Your Creation can press birthday cake pieces, brownie chunks, candy, and fruit into every fold, exactly to order. The shop is small and seating sits outside, so grab a cup and stroll CityWalk with it. Brownie a la Cold Stone, a hot brownie under cold scoops, suits a long park night. Come for customization performed at the counter.

places.name: Se7en Bites
places.address: 617 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A spa industry veteran followed her grandmother's recipes to culinary school, and the Milk District noticed. Se7en Bites drew Guy Fieri and Triple D attention, plus a Michelin nod in its record, and lines followed. The chicken pot pie vanishes quickly, the Vanilla Bean Bourbon Bacon Moon Pie is the legend, and the Minnie Pearl chicken and waffles and Se7enth Heaven smash burger back up the sweets. Come early, because regulars know the popular trays and plates sell out.

places.name: Kelly's Homemade Ice Cream
places.address: 3114 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Orlando-made and proud of it, Kelly's churns small-batch ice cream across a string of scoop shops. Monthly flavors read like a dessert diary: bear claw, fluffernutter, hummingbird cake, and toasted s'mores. Clear labeling covers allergies, non-dairy flavors rotate in, and Dog Pops serve four-legged regulars. The Fern Creek shop runs patio karaoke nights, which tells you plenty about the vibe. Warm and playful, the shops make leaving with one scoop difficult. Choose Kelly's when local ice cream should feel personal, changing, and neighborhood-rooted.

places.name: The Stubborn Mule
places.address: 100 S Eola Dr #103, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: One block from the swans of Lake Eola, a New American spot built around the Moscow Mule's swagger: hand-crafted mule cocktails, hyper-local drafts, and a kitchen run by Culinary Institute graduates with farm and fisherman relationships to prove it. The Stubborn Mule Burger wears Havarti fondue, the waffle burger sandwiches savory beef between two sweet waffles, and the sticky pork belly and parmesan rosemary fries have their own fan club. Eat too much, then stroll it off around the lake.

places.name: Jesse's Rib Shack
places.address: 2202 W Pine St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Smoke has hung over this West Pine shack since long before barbecue became a trend. The late Jesse Jackson opened Jesse's Rib Shack in 1987, and his grandson Jamaal keeps the smoke and the cooking where they belong. Ribs and chicken ride on the homemade Magic Sauce, a recipe locals describe as drinkable, and the creamy mac and cheese has its own following. Doors stay open until the food sells out, and it sells out, so arrive with patience and an appetite.

places.name: The Villa
places.address: 25 Wall St Bldg B, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Arcade games by day and cocktails after dark share one Wall Street Plaza room. The Villa runs modern arcade games, board game tables, and video game stations that welcome families early. After dark, the room shifts to an adult playground of cocktails, bites, and pop hits, with winnings trading for food and drinks and Orlando City matches on the screens. Choose it for game night with a grown up edge, especially when your group cannot agree on one kind of entertainment.

places.name: Croissant Gourmet
places.address: 120 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Two French brothers brought a small piece of France to Winter Park. Francois, a classically trained patissier, leads a case built from scratch each morning, with the almond croissant as the star: flaky layers around sweet almond paste, dusted with confectioners sugar. Fruit tarts, eclairs, Napoleons, macarons, and the raspberry jalousie run deep, while lunch turns savory with a croque madame whose golden yolk runs down the sandwich. Go when pastry should taste trained, patient, and unmistakably French.

places.name: Junior Colombian Burger
places.address: 11875 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Colombian street food hijacks the American burger here, and the result refuses to be quiet. The Explosion Burger stacks plantain, mozzarella, egg, corn, and potato sticks into something glorious and unapologetic. The Triple piles crushed chips and house pineapple sauce, while the Burger Dog goes full Bogota with pineapple and pink sauce. Papas locas, homemade empanadas, and signature garlic and pink sauces cover the rest of the table. Open late for night owls, it earns the line locals use when they call it the best burger in Orlando.

places.name: U & Me Revolving Hot Pot
places.address: 12384 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Hot pot meets a conveyor belt, and dinner turns into a game you play at the table. U & Me lets you pick a broth, bone, beef, mushroom, Sichuan heat, or Thai Tom Yum, then pull fresh plates from the revolving line. Thin sliced beef, seafood, and vegetables drop into the pot as you choose them. A sauce bar is yours to customize, the boba tea menu holds up, and robot waiters deliver drinks while a sassy one seats you. Choose it for all you can eat fun that leaves kids delighted and adults stuffed.

places.name: Chewy Boba Company
places.address: 1212 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Bubble tea was still exotic in Orlando when this family business started pouring in 2002. Chewy Boba keeps the Colonial Drive shop classic with taro milk tea, passionfruit, and brown sugar milk in generous cups at honest prices. The University Boulevard outpost adds a tap served boba system and fresh sugarcane juice guests call criminally refreshing in Florida heat. Vietnamese iced coffee with sea salt cold foam and seasonal specials round out the menu. Choose Chewy when you want long running boba craft with both classic cups and newer experiments.

places.name: Hard Rock Live
places.address: 6050 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Three thousand people, and somehow every seat feels close to the stage. Hard Rock Live delivers concerts, stand-up and big touring names with arena-grade sound and lighting in a room with the intimacy of a club. It sits beside the Hard Rock Cafe at CityWalk, so the memorabilia is everywhere: Elvis's suit, smashed guitars, a museum of loud. Check the calendar before your CityWalk night, because the lineup decides the evening. For a touring show without arena distance, this room is hard to beat.

places.name: Inter.co Stadium
places.address: 655 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Downtown's soccer cathedral, home to Orlando City SC and the Orlando Pride since 2017. On match nights the stands turn purple, the drumline never stops, and twenty-five thousand voices make the downtown air shake. The Orlando Made concessions program stocks the concourses with local favorites, and the building has hosted World Cup qualifiers, an MLS All-Star Game, and the Special Olympics opening ceremony. Even if you're not a football purist, one match night here converts you.

places.name: Orlando Farmers Market
places.address: 20 N Eola Dr, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Every Sunday, the Lake Eola lakefront turns into downtown Orlando's weekly ritual, a market running since 1987. Produce and prepared foods share space with artisan stalls and handmade goods, while a wine and beer garden handles the grown ups and live music drifts across the lakefront. Dogs are welcome, swan boats glide past and themed Sundays keep the routine fresh. Bring a tote, bring the dog and stay a while. The city shops, strolls and eats here on its day of rest.

places.name: Marlow's Tavern
places.address: 6889 Eagle Watch Dr, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: The neighborhood tavern that took itself seriously in the kitchen. Scratch-made American fare with a chef's ambition: firecracker shrimp with cracklin' and sweet chili, J.T.'s kettle chips crowned with gorgonzola and bacon, shrimp and crab nachos that surprise everyone, and shrimp and grits on a white cheddar grit cake. The bar pours craft cocktails alongside the classics. Lively, warm, and the kind of place where the server remembers your order by the second visit.

places.name: Yard House
places.address: 8367 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A wall of a hundred plus tap handles and a glass enclosed keg room holding thousands of gallons of fresh beer set the tone at ICON Park. Classic rock plays on the speakers and the crowd came to share. The menu runs globally inspired: poke nachos, a Korean BBQ cheesesteak, and a tower of onion rings built for the table. Portions run big and the energy follows. Come here when the night on I-Drive needs another chapter and your group cannot agree on one cuisine.

places.name: Bubba Gump Shrimp Co.
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd Ste 735, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Shrimp arrives every way Bubba named in the movie, with trivia under your plate. Bubba Gump serves fried shrimp, coconut shrimp, peel-and-eat shrimp, and shrimp mac and cheese at Universal CityWalk. Southern comfort covers other appetites: baby back ribs, fried chicken, and homemade desserts. Staff keep the show going throughout the meal. Take the photo in the Forrest Gump running shoes out front and find the bus bench. It is touristy, knows it, and serves shrimp that is genuinely good. Give in to the theme completely.

places.name: The Cheesecake Factory
places.address: 4200 Conroy Rd Space A-148, Orlando, FL 32839
places.description: The menu reads like a novel, and somehow the kitchen pulls it off. The Cheesecake Factory lists more than two hundred fifty items made from scratch at the Mall at Millenia. Start with avocado eggrolls or Thai lettuce wraps, move to orange chicken or the Factory burger, and save room for more than thirty cheesecakes, from the original to toasted marshmallow s'mores. Weekend brunch adds a fried chicken and waffle benedict. Choose the patio when Florida sun suits the meal, and come with a group that orders widely.

places.name: The Donut King
places.address: 3716 Howell Branch Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A family-run donut shop makes chains easy to forget by morning. The Donut King turns out soft, pillowy donuts bigger than you expect, fried fresh in-house daily. Maple bacon glazed is the cult favorite, apple fritters sell out if you sleep in, and cases run from red velvet glazed to blueberry cake and candy-bar toppings. Prices stay affordable by the dozen, which makes sharing simple. Get there early for fritters, and treat this Winter Park stop as the neighborhood morning ritual it has become for regulars.

places.name: Kilwins Ice Cream - Chocolate - Fudge
places.address: 122 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Caramel finds you first on Park Avenue, before the case even comes into view. Kilwins works as old-school confectionery theater: fudge paddled on a marble slab in the open kitchen, caramel apples dipped and dressed in front of you, and heritage chocolate going back to 1947. Super-premium ice cream in a hand-crafted waffle cone headlines the visit, but turtle fudge and caramel apples explain why people leave with a box. Come for sweets made visibly, slowly, and with a Winter Park stroll waiting outside.

places.name: Winter Park Farmers Market
places.address: 150 N New York Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Saturday morning belongs to Central Park West Meadow in Winter Park. The farmers market spreads out with Central Florida produce, artisan breads, local honey, fresh flowers, seafood and specialty bites from Jamaican patties to kettle popcorn. It works as a genuine community gathering: dog friendly, strollable and steps from Park Avenue shopping. Locals call it their weekly ritual, and one visit shows why. Come hungry, arrive early and leave with flowers, because the meadow rewards a slow lap.

places.name: The Ganachery
places.address: The Ganachery, 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Disney Springs treats chocolate as craft rather than souvenir here. The Ganachery's expert chocolatiers work an open show kitchen, cutting ganache squares in sixteen flavors, torching artisan s'mores to order, and making ganache pops and chocolate piñatas filled with treats. The program uses single-origin dark chocolate from the Dominican Republic, old-world techniques, fresh cream, and real vanilla beans. Mickey and Minnie chocolate bars suit kids, while dark chocolate with Egyptian salt suits you. Every bite feels crafted because the process stays visible.

places.name: BakeChop
places.address: 110 Artisan Aly, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: A scratch kitchen on Artisan Alley is where DeLand gives farm-to-table real conviction. BakeChop serves the Left Hander burger and a Peach Jam Burger with goat cheese and jalapeños that guests call otherworldly. The Fish Bowl appears as a day's special, collard greens draw regular demand, and a quinoa salad steals attention it had no obvious claim to. The family motto centers food, family, friends, service, and good times, and plates reflect that list. Choose it when you want a DeLand meal built from scratch.

places.name: Donuts To Go
places.address: 502 N Spring Garden Ave, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: An early-morning sweet spot leads with a square donut built for sharing. Donuts To Go serves a generously sized Square Glazed Donut alongside Maple Bacon, French Toast, Almond Joy, and a flaky Cronut. Chocolate cake donuts draw fans who call them heavenly, and caramel work gets its own praise. Breakfast widens the visit: burritos, biscuits and gravy, and New York-style bagels with cream cheese. Fresh, homemade, and kid-friendly, the shop earns local loyalty. Come hungry enough to take donuts and a real breakfast seriously together.

places.name: The Crooked Spoon
places.address: 200 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711
places.description: A beloved Orlando food truck grew up without losing its hunger. Now a Clermont gastropub, The Crooked Spoon serves Chef Saelg's bold menu, from the 420 Burger with candied bacon and pineapple relish to lobster grilled cheese and six-cheese lobster mac. Polynesian pig wings widen the range, and blue cheese chips are legendary among regulars. A full bar, outdoor seating, and a room that feels like the neighborhood's living room complete it. Pick it for foodie ambition carried by small-town heart, in Clermont rather than downtown.

places.name: Over The Top Pita
places.address: Over the Top Pita, 240 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711-2704
places.description: Fast food does not have to taste fast at this family owned pita shop. Warm pita holds gyro sliced right off the spit, crisp vegetables and bold sauces stacked until the wrap barely closes. Every order is made to order, with the classic Gyro Pita as the standard move and loaded pitas for the truly hungry. The room runs on no corporate kitchen warmth from people proud of what they serve. Choose it when a quick lunch should still feel made for you.

places.name: Reunion Resort & Golf Club
places.address: 7593 Gathering Dr, Kissimmee, FL 34747
places.description: Three signature courses drawn by Palmer, Watson and Nicklaus, and each one feels like its own world of fairways. But Reunion is bigger than golf: sprawling villas and vacation homes, a water park with lazy river and slides, tennis and pickleball, and the rooftop restaurant Eleven where you can watch fireworks bloom over the parks. Bring the buddies for the tee times, bring the whole family for everything else, and never once feel like leaving the gates.

places.name: Swine & Sons
places.address: 201 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Milk District sandwich craft gets obsessive in the right hands at Swine and Sons. Born from the Petrakis family's Ravenous Pig roots and now run by chefs Rhys and Alexia Gawlak, the shop runs the kitchen at The Milkhouse on Bumby Avenue. House cured charcuterie leads the case, Nashville Hot Chicken is the sandwich regulars plan a week around, and a smash burger stops conversation at the table. Grab a table and order boldly. Choose Swine and Sons when you want serious sandwich work, and save room for the Oatmeal Cream Pie.

places.name: Foxtail Coffee
places.address: 2401 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: A hometown coffee company can grow across a city and still pour like a neighbor. Foxtail started as one small Orlando shop and became a local institution while keeping an unhurried, neighborly warmth at each location. Espresso stays serious, cold brew flights turn tasting into a ritual, and seasonal drinks lean playful without feeling gimmicky. You can bring the dog for a pup cup, camp with a laptop, and watch the city run on caffeine. Choose Foxtail when you want Orlando coffee done right, without rushing the people drinking it.

places.name: First Watch
places.address: 11951 International Drive South Ste A, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Morning matters at this Bradenton born breakfast brand, and the kitchen proves it plate by plate. Everything is made to order in a kitchen with no heat lamps, no microwaves, and no fryers. The menu gives you Floridian French Toast, Million Dollar Bacon, smoked salmon eggs benedict, fresh pressed juices, and Project Sunrise coffee. Bright rooms and sunlit patios suit the one shift the restaurant works each day. Choose First Watch when you want brunch that feels deliberate, fresh, and built around the morning rather than stretched across the whole day.

places.name: Le Macaron French Pastries Winter Park
places.address: 216 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A courtyard off Park Avenue hides a little piece of Paris in Winter Park. Le Macaron serves macarons with crisp shells and soft centers, colored like a jewel box, from classic Belgian chocolate to lavender white chocolate. French gelato, eclairs, Napoleons, beignets, and European-style drinks extend the case beyond one cookie. The setting feels tucked away without being hard to enjoy. Walk in for one and leave with a box when you can, because a small assortment travels well and pleases almost everyone.

places.name: 1881 Restaurant & Bar
places.address: 1881 Restaurant, 308 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34741-5718
places.description: Downtown Kissimmee hides an Uzbek, Turkish and Mediterranean kitchen inside a historic hardware building. The 1881 Restaurant and Bar fills the Makinson Hardware building on Broadway with steaming manti dumplings, hand pulled lagman noodles and fragrant pilaf studded with beef and lamb. A mixed grill is built for the table, and a full bar plus welcoming outdoor seating round out the room. Come curious and order dishes you cannot pronounce yet. Few corners of Central Florida cooking feel this unexpected.

places.name: Dang Boba & Musubi House
places.address: Dang Boba & Musubi House, 11772 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4625
places.description: Two cravings share one roof here, and the pairing makes sense by the second sip. Run by UCF alumni, Dang Boba and Musubi House brews teas with care through its Bobaristas: lavender milk tea, tiger tea, and princess peach fruit tea. Then musubi stack like edible architecture in classic spam, spam and kimchi, and garlic soy chicken versions. The room stays cheerful and student friendly, with dessert and dining under the same sign. Choose Dang when boba culture and Hawaiian comfort food sound better together than apart, which they do here.

places.name: Grape & the Grain
places.address: Grape & the Grain, 1110 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Staff who remember your pour make a wine bar feel like a neighborhood room. Grape and the Grain in Mills 50 pours wines hand selected from vineyards across the globe, with Florida craft beer for the non wine crowd and a charcuterie board built for lingering. Out back, a covered patio adds funky art, food trucks, trivia nights, and DJs. Novices and connoisseurs get the same welcome and zero pretension. Choose it when you want to slow down without the evening going quiet.

places.name: Bento Sushi
places.address: Bento Sushi, 12715 Pegasus Dr, Orlando, FL 32816-8030
places.description: BENTO's pan-Asian kitchens are Orlando's reliable answer to the question of where everyone can agree. Sushi rolls cut fresh, poke bowls built your way, hearty bento boxes with teriyaki and katsu, Thai curries for the spice-seekers, plus boba teas to finish. Fast, friendly, and generous with portions, the kind of spot that works for a quick lunch, a family dinner, or the group chat that could never pick a place.

places.name: Juice Bar
places.address: Juice Bar, 2413 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803-6324
places.description: A plain name hides East South Street's longtime temple of fresh juice. Juice Bar makes cold-pressed blends to order on a Norwalk juicer, with playful names like Hale to the Kale and Gangsta Green. The all-vegan menu adds smoothies and acai bowls that regulars swear by. Everything tastes like actual fruit because, the record says, it is. Free parking sits out front and zero pretense waits inside. Come when you want juice pressed to order, a vegan bowl alongside it, and no performance beyond freshness.

places.name: Matt's Latin BBQ
places.address: Matt's Latin BBQ, 6607 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Mofongo gets smashed to order while pernil and ribs wait over rice and beans. Matt's Latin BBQ on South Semoran cooks campo style, bringing island cooking into the city with rotisserie chicken, ropa vieja, and morcilla seasoned from freshly ground ingredients. The decor feels like Puerto Rico, the kitchen keeps moving, and regulars will tell you the mofongo is the best in town. Come hungry and expect to leave feeling like family, especially if Puerto Rican comfort food is your language.

places.name: Sly Fox
places.address: Sly Fox, 63 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2425
places.description: Punk rock upstairs energy and a basement stage keep downtown's dive tradition loud. Sly Fox pours cold beer through late nights while local music runs below, then surprises you with food: vegan hot dogs and burgers from the Vegan Hot Dog Cart, plus loaded tater tots and late night comfort plates. The room is gritty, warm, and completely itself, a home base for Orlando's alternative scene. Go when you want to exhale somewhere unpolished, hear a band, and eat better than a dive bar has to serve.

places.name: TooJay's
places.address: 2624 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Florida's New York-style deli has kept its nostalgic spread since 1981. TooJay's on Colonial Drive serves towering pastrami and Reuben sandwiches, matzo ball soup, and blintzes. A bakery case holds rugalach, babka, and the famous Killer Cake. Portions run big, service moves fast and friendly, and the menu offers that particular deli joy of eating three meals without repeating yourself. Bring an appetite and a takeout bag, because the bakery case rarely lets a table leave empty-handed after sandwiches that size.

places.name: Fujiyama Sushi
places.address: Fujiyama Sushi, 10153 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: A UCF-area staple for sushi that respects both your cravings and your wallet. The menu covers both routes without forcing a choice. Volcano rolls, Philly rolls, teppan lunches sizzling on the griddle, bento boxes packed with teriyaki and tempura, plus tempura cheesecake for the finish. The room is unfussy and friendly, the fish is fresh, and it's the rare sushi spot that works just as well for a study-break lunch as for a full dinner with friends.

places.name: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen
places.address: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027
places.description: Chef Tuvi brings over 20 years of Thai technique to an unassuming Oviedo plaza, and the neighborhood knows what it found. Panang duck, lobster phad thai, tamarind shrimp and whole snapper dinners people still talk about months later lead the menu, with housemade sauces throughout. Durian ice cream waits for the adventurous at the end. The room is contemporary and calm, the flavors are bright and true, and the cooking carries real depth. For Oviedo Thai that goes beyond the standard takeout rotation, Lemongrass is the address.

places.name: Stefano's Trattoria
places.address: Stefano's Trattoria, 1425 Tuskawilla Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708-4703
places.description: A family-owned Italian kitchen on Tuskawilla Road has served Winter Springs for two decades, and the experience shows in small details. Gnocchi della nonna in pink sauce, veal piccata, and lobster ravioli anchor a menu that closes well with a tiramisu cheesecake worth saving room for. Live piano drifts across the dining room while the owner still works the floor, greeting guests in a way that makes the table feel personally hosted. You come for a neighborhood dinner and get what real Italian hospitality tastes like: unhurried, familiar, and generous.

places.name: White Rabbit Dessert Experience
places.address: White Rabbit Dessert Experience, 875 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828-7049
places.description: Dessert becomes a full evening out in Waterford Lakes if you follow the rabbit. White Rabbit offers over 100 made-to-order creations from a modern open kitchen: waffles, crepes, towering sundaes, cakes, and brownies, crowned with homemade ice cream made fresh daily. The space is designed for indulgence, and an espresso bar keeps adults happy while the table decides. Variety is the practical draw for mixed groups. Visit when dessert deserves its own plan, not an afterthought squeezed in after dinner elsewhere in Orlando.

places.name: Broken Strings Taproom
places.address: Broken Strings Brewery, 1012 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805-2216
places.description: Two breweries share one roof on West Church Street, and live music sits in the DNA of the room. Murals of music legends cover the taproom walls while the stage hosts reggae nights, local bands, open mics, and DJ sets. The beer lineup leans playful with Penny Layne strawberry blonde, Purple Mane pale ale, and Liquid Vinyl. The space is pet friendly and game day ready, reopened under local ownership with community spirit intact. Choose Broken Strings when you want your pint paired with a stage, a mural wall, and a crowd.

places.name: Clean Eatz
places.address: Clean Eatz, 2205 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32806-3038
places.description: Healthy food rarely gets to keep this much flavor, but this SoDo cafe tries. Clean Eatz builds bowls to order and serves a Bang Bang Shrimp Wrap, Monterey Chicken, and buffalo chicken wraps in tomato-basil tortillas. Weekly meal plans and grab-and-go cases cover dinners beyond the visit. Every menu item lists its calories, so you can choose with the numbers in front of you. Come here when you want a health-food lunch that stays informed rather than guilty, and practical enough to repeat during a busy week.

places.name: Maple Street Biscuit Company
places.address: Maple Street Biscuit Company, 11810 Glass House Ln, Orlando, FL 32836-3794
places.description: A biscuit can carry a whole menu when every one is baked from scratch daily. Maple Street builds Southern comfort on hand breaded chicken and signatures with cult followings. The Squawking Goat pairs fried goat cheese with fried chicken, while the Five and Dime and smashbrowns with sausage gravy keep the table busy. Fried green tomatoes round out the plate, and a maple vanilla latte fits the room naturally. Settle onto the patio and you understand why this Florida born company keeps growing beyond its first kitchens and counters.

places.name: Sushi Yama
places.address: Sushi Yama, 6748 Grand National Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-8526
places.description: All-you-can-eat sushi on International Drive anchors Sushi Yama, with a lineup deep enough to reward ordering in waves. Dragon rolls, rainbow rolls, and crazy yellowtail cover the rolls, while thick-cut sashimi and yellowtail jalapeno keep the raw side interesting. Hibachi steak and fried rice widen the table, and fried tempura cheesecake waits at the end for anyone who paced the early rounds well. Lines form for a reason, and the room suits groups who eat at different speeds. Bring an empty stomach and pace yourself like the pros at the next table.

places.name: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen
places.address: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen, 6125 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822-1500
places.description: Fresh plates of ono grindz near the airport draw devotees who praise the cooking highly. The Aloha Special stacks crispy pork belly, ono shrimp, and mochiko chicken over rice. Kalbi, huli huli chicken, and loco moco arrive in generous portions with mac salad alongside. Save room for Alohasadas, doughnuts filled with ube, haupia, and pandan. The room reads friendly and clean, with a warm island feel. Come hungry for a Hawaiian plate lunch, and let the filled doughnuts settle what you order for dessert.

places.name: Black Magic Pizza
places.address: Black Magic Pizza, 121 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The self-proclaimed punk rock pizza wizards of the Milk District started as a pandemic pop-up and became one of Orlando's most talked-about slices. Their hand-tossed pies are neither New York nor Neapolitan but somewhere in between: the Dr. Pepperoni, the Hornets Nest with hot honey and soppressata, and the Tuscan Leather. Dough is made in small batches, flavors take risks, and vegan options do not feel like an afterthought. Order the pie that sounds strangest; at Black Magic, that instinct usually pays off.

places.name: City Food Hall
places.address: City Food Hall, 1412 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803-1862
places.description: Indecision is the ideal condition at the Hall on the Yard by Lake Formosa. A curated mix of local concepts circles one big roof: smash burgers, street tacos on hand pressed tortillas, New Orleans po'boys, shrimp and grits, fresh sushi and New York style bagels. A central bar pours seasonal cocktails and local taps, Topgolf Swing Suites sit upstairs, and live events fill the outdoor plaza. Dinner becomes a whole evening here, especially when your group refuses to agree on one cuisine.

places.name: Crocante Restaurant
places.address: Crocante Restaurant, 4311 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5217
places.description: Puerto Rican cooking gets the full restaurant and cocktail bar treatment on East Colonial. Executive chef Yamuel Bigio makes slow roasted porchetta the signature, cooking it until the name Crocante makes sense. Around it, the menu rewards curiosity with bacalaitos tacos, bistec encebollado eggrolls, chicharron with guacamole and shrimp mofongo. Tembeleque handles dessert for the table. Choose Crocante when you want Boricua flavors dressed for a night out, with crunch running through the meal from start to finish.

places.name: Chicken Fire
places.address: Chicken Fire, 2425 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5018
places.description: Nashville style hot chicken with soul, served from a no frills joint on East Colonial. The kitchen uses never frozen tenderloins, brined for up to 24 hours, hand breaded and fried to order, then tossed in your chosen heat level, from gentle Soulful to straight fire. The Hot Box piles on crinkle cut fries, coleslaw and the signature Soul Sauce, while the mega sliders are a two fisted commitment. Order it when you want crispy, fiery chicken made with obvious care, and pick your heat level honestly.

places.name: Empanada & Co.
places.address: Empanada & Co., 15 E 5th St, Apopka, FL 32703-5244
places.description: Baked, golden and made from scratch, the empanadas in Apopka pull ingredients from local small businesses. The lineup runs from chicken and cheese, Cuban and picadillo to smoked gouda and mushroom. Dessert turns to guava and queso or banana Nutella, and housemade sauces do real work: green chile tomatillo, Ecuadorian hot and cilantro garlic mayo. Quick service keeps it easy, while the flaky crusts keep it specific. Order across sweet and savory, because choosing only one style undersells the case.

places.name: Kavas Tacos & Tequila
places.address: 9101 International Dr Ste 1198, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Pointe Orlando gets its loudest welcome at this colorful taco bar on International Drive. Quesabirria tacos come dripping with consomme, a three-foot taco board is built for the whole table, and carnitas flautas round out the shareable end of the menu. The margarita list includes watermelon and the Kadillac, nightly live entertainment, DJs and fire shows keep the room moving, and weekend brunch gives you a second reason to come. Choose it for a convention crowd that wants dinner and a party in one stop.

places.name: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf
places.address: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf, 3402 Technological Ave, Orlando, FL 32817-1402
places.description: Ramen comes with a side of theater near UCF. The bowls are the main act: Tokyo tonkotsu shoyu, Kyushu spicy tonkotsu, the yin-yang bowl with two broths in one, plus fluffy tonkotsu omurice and pork belly bao. The room leans playful, with treehouse-like seating, private honeycomb booths and curtain-drawn date tables that make dinner feel staged in a good way. Finish with TBaar bubble tea or matcha pudding. Choose Kyuramen when the group wants a photogenic ramen night near campus, not just a quick bowl.

places.name: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant
places.address: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant, 933 Orlando Ave S, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Lim Ros means "to taste" in Thai, and this modern Maitland dining room makes sure you do plenty of it. Crying tiger steak earns its name, kanom jeen namya pu brings a house curry brimming with real crabmeat, and tom kha gai arrives as a hot pot. The panang curry draws regular praise, and a full gluten-free and vegan menu widens the table. Butterfly pea tea cocktails and upscale but unpretentious service complete the picture. Pick it for a Maitland dinner where dietary needs and big flavor both matter.

places.name: Melt N Dip
places.address: 7341 W Sand Lake Rd Ste 1081, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Belgian chocolate, warm and gooey, coats nearly everything in this Dubai-born dessert house. Melt N Dip serves stuffed crepes dripping with sauce, fresh-baked brownies, crispy waffle sticks, thick milkshakes, gelato, and fresh fruit platters with chocolate dips on Sand Lake. The menu runs enormous, the chocolate rich, and the room family-friendly by design. One visit can satisfy whatever sweet tooth brought you in. Choose it when your group cannot agree on dessert, because crepes, waffles, fruit, and gelato all arrive under one chocolate logic.

places.name: Oza Izakaya
places.address: Oza Izakaya, 5310 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-8772
places.description: A modern Japanese izakaya in Metrowest pairs sleek garden styling with a chef, Tim Liu, cooking like every plate is a first date. Yuzu hamachi, buttery uni toast, wagyu gyoza with truffle, grilled octopus with yuzu foam, and miso yaki cod give a table plenty to pass around. An excellent sake list and nightly cocktails support the plan rather than distract from it. The room is built for lingering under the garden lights, with small plates setting an unhurried pace. You order small, share everything, and let the night stretch out.

places.name: Smokey Jay's BBQ
places.address: Smokey Jay's BBQ, 9318 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4100
places.description: Good bark takes time, and the pit starts before dawn here. Smokey Jay's smokes over real wood until the bark and smoke ring are right, serving ribs described as fall off the bone, tender pulled pork, and brisket loaded fries. Collard greens, candied yams, and homemade mac and cheese fill out the plate, with red velvet cake at the end. The family run operation has a devoted following and stays open until sold out, so earlier is the safer plan.

places.name: Sushi Pop
places.address: Sushi Pop, 310 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765-4921
places.description: Oviedo gets a monotony breaker at Sushi Pop, where Chef Chau runs the sushi bar like an artist's studio. Seasonal crudo, nikkei maki, ceviche rolls, and buffalo rock shrimp show the range, and an omakase is worth trusting him with when you want the kitchen to lead. The room feels like a Vegas tourist district in the best way: bold, loud, and unapologetic about either. Seafood freshness is the kitchen's calling card, presented without quieting the room down. Book ahead, because this one gets packed, and plan to order beyond your usual roll.

places.name: Ten10 Brewing
places.address: Ten10 Brewing, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2532
places.description: A tasting room works best when friends and strangers actually meet there, and Ten10 lives that idea in Mills 50. The self styled DIY punk rock brew crew pours character driven beers including Grandmas Purse butterscotch ale. Big Green Egg smoked wings and a kitchen that punches above its weight give the taproom a food reason too. A dog friendly patio, Tuesday run club, Thursday trivia, and live music keep the calendar social. Choose Ten10 when you want neighborhood brewing at its happiest, with a pint and a patio waiting for you.

places.name: The Escobar Kitchen
places.address: The Escobar Kitchen, 420 E Church St, Orlando, FL 32801-2775
places.description: Latin flavors meet sushi rolls here, and the combination is bolder than you might expect. Family owned in South Eola, the kitchen builds the Escobar Roll with shrimp tempura, churrasco and sweet plantains, then tops the Mar Y Tierra with chimichurri. The Paisa Roll and Gentleman's Roll keep regulars loyal, while the signature Arroz Enchurrascado works like paella style rice with skirt steak, plantains and chimichurri. Order it when you want sushi that refuses to play it quiet.

places.name: TT Crepes
places.address: TT Crepes, 10681 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4470
places.description: A supermarket counter can hide the best kind of surprise when the menu stays small. Inside Mei Supermarket in Union Park, TT Crepes focuses on jianbing, the Chinese street crepe with crisp, egg laced crunch. Scallion pancakes get done right beside it, and regulars know exactly what they are getting from the dialed in flavors. The counter stays unassuming and free of pretension from the first order. Choose TT Crepes when you want a focused street food stop where crunch, egg, and scallion do the talking.

places.name: Vinia Wine & Kitchen
places.address: Vinia Wine & Kitchen, 444 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4224
places.description: You get welcomed like a guest at home, and dinner keeps that same warmth. Husband and wife Fabio Perricelli and Paula Gamba run this Hannibal Square wine bar with Italian and Brazilian soul. Shared plates include braised oxtail gnocchi, Romeu and Julieta cheese bread with guava sauce, vegan escargot, and beet wellington. A curated boutique wine list, low light, and live music complete the room. Vinia earned Critic's Choice for Best Vegan/Vegetarian in the 2025 Orlando Sentinel Foodie Awards, and carnivores still eat very well here.

places.name: AJ Chocolate House
places.address: AJ Chocolate House, 552 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4322, United States
places.description: A European-rooted chocolate shop on Park Avenue blends luxury with edible art. AJ Chocolate House serves Belgian truffles, molten fondues, and a charcuterie tower built for sharing. Waffles arrive ready to dip in chocolate, fig and salmon crostinis widen the menu, and wine and coffee round out an evening. Guests praise the owner as warm and attentive, and Executive Chef Edwin Jablonskas runs the kitchen. A second location recently opened in New Smyrna Beach. Come to Winter Park when chocolate should be an outing, not an afterthought.

places.name: Boku Sushi
places.address: Boku Sushi, 140 Independence Ln, Maitland, FL 32751-5603, United States
places.description: Tucked into the corner of its Maitland complex behind the Starbucks, Boku is the kind of neighborhood sushi spot that makes regulars out of first-timers. The room glows with warm wood, tile and stone, and the rolls have cult followings: the Drama Queen, the Foxy Lady, the Out of Control, and a jalapeño hamachi one reviewer swore was the best version he had ever tasted. Sit out on the pet-friendly patio when the evening cools, and ask about the Sea Bass.

places.name: Schakolad Chocolate Factory
places.address: Schakolad Chocolate Factory, 9901 Hawaiian Ct, Orlando, FL 32819-8102, United States
places.description: Pronounce it shaq-oh-LAD, then look at the cases and prepare to linger. Schakolad began when Edgar Schaked left an engineering career to keep his father Baruch's chocolatier legacy alive. The Orlando factory makes European-style chocolates fresh on the premises daily, with more than seventy varieties of truffles, molded novelties, wedding favors, and edible gift creations. Sweet Night Out events let you go behind the counter to make and decorate your own, with generous taste testing along the way. Come for a family story told in chocolate.

places.name: Half Barrel Beer Project
places.address: Half Barrel Beer Project, 9650 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-8766, United States
places.description: Small room, serious beer obsession, and no reason to judge by size. Half Barrel squeezes a twelve tap room onto Universal Boulevard, with two house brews pouring beside a curated selection of Florida craft. Coolers stack deep with bottles and cans to take home, and staff talk beer the way regulars do. The room stays industrial and unpretentious, and fall off the bone wings have a following of their own. Choose Half Barrel when you want a craft beer stop that rewards browsing, tasting, and taking a few bottles with you.

places.name: Mario's Pizza
places.address: Mario's Pizza, 7213 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32822-5805, United States
places.description: A Curry Ford corner spot does New York style the honest way. Dough is made fresh daily, cheese is cut fresh daily, and produce comes from a local distributor at Mario's, where the menu stretches from calzones and strombolis to baked pasta and ziti. The owner is known to sit down and talk with guests, and the vegan side punches above its weight, from the Girlfriend pie to the Crown Jewel. It is a neighborhood family joint that treats a slice like it matters, and regulars notice that care.

places.name: Pienezza Pizza
places.address: Pienezza Pizza, 3236 N John Young Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741-7549, United States
places.description: Generations of Brooklyn tradition set the table at this family-owned Kissimmee pizzeria, and you can taste the borough in every fold of the crust. Beyond the classic round pies, the signatures tell the story: the Hey Brooklyn, the Crazy Margherita, a Sicilian Flag layered with red and white sauces, and a Grandma's pie that regulars swear transports them straight to the city. A second spot in Downtown Orlando's Creative Village spreads the family further. Order the Grandma's first if you want the regulars' argument in edible form.

places.name: San Julian's Coffee
places.address: San Julian's Coffee, 110 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-3656, United States
places.description: Winter Park has no shortage of coffee shops, but none pour quite like San Julián's. This cozy Colombian coffee bar on Orlando Avenue brews the way the Andes intended: rich, smooth, unapologetically strong, with standouts like the pistachio latte and the viral tiramisu latte. The food menu reads like a love letter to Colombia and Venezuela, with arepas, empanadas, crispy tequeños, and flaky guava-and-cheese quesitos. Mornings simply taste better here, and the regulars will tell you so.

places.name: Sushi Lola's
places.address: Sushi Lola's, 2902 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803, United States
places.description: Sushi Lola's runs on a delicious split personality. Owner Aaron Pak has kept two kitchens humming on Corrine Drive in Audubon Park for over a decade: one for sushi, one for Korean, so your table can hold a Playboy roll and a sizzling dolsot bibimbap at once. The Lava Dips are a cult appetizer, the Volcano roll lives up to its name, and dessert arrives as a warm browned butter cookie, on the house. It is the rare fusion spot where both halves of the hyphen earn their keep.

places.name: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry
places.address: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry, 1436 State Road 436, Casselberry, FL 32707-6506, United States
places.description: Founder Freddy Zubieta started cooking at fifteen, and that lifelong obsession reached Orlando by food truck in 2015. The Casselberry outpost belongs to a fleet now stretching to Tampa and Sarasota. Ceviche anchors the visit in several forms, from classic to Carretilla, with leche de tigre, the fiery citrus marinade regulars drink straight. Lomo Saltado, crispy jalea, and a proper pisco sour complete the route. Choose it when you want Peruvian coastal flavors with heat, acid, and enough variety to build a table-wide tasting.

places.name: Hinode Sushi
places.address: Hinode Sushi, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027, United States
places.description: Chef George Tan plates sushi like art in this Oviedo neighborhood spot, and locals treat it as their own delicious secret. The Trio Tower stacks tuna, salmon, yellowtail, mango and avocado into something striking, the Black Widow roll wears a spiderweb of sauce, and even the avocado fries arrive as beautiful little sculptures. Everything tastes as vivid as it looks, from the Roll On Fire to the Oviedo Sunrise. A warm, family-run room where the fish is always fresh and the plates always turn heads.

places.name: Ollie's Public House
places.address: Ollie's Public House, 3400 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-3602, United States
places.description: College Park asks for everything at once, and Ollie's tries to hand it over. The Edgewater Drive public house pairs a rotating craft beer list with more than thirty TVs, live music, and a big covered patio where dogs get water and cold cuts by name. Regulars swear by the Legend sandwich and the Wall Street Reuben, bar food runs deep, and a rotating Good Bite menu item gives back to a local cause. Pick it when a weeknight needs a room that refuses to be boring.

places.name: Tropico Mofongo
places.address: Tropico Mofongo, 3160 Vineland Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34746-4657, United States
places.description: The name is the menu's thesis in Kissimmee: plantains, chicharron and garlic, pounded into mofongo. Tropico Mofongo serves it under pernil, shrimp or all three in the Mofongo Trio, which locals call the best in town. The bright, cheerful room keeps music upbeat, the pernil sandwich with pickled onions works as a sleeper hit, and regulars insist the mojitos and margaritas are the area's finest. Generous portions and Puerto Rican soul make it worth choosing deliberately.

places.name: Bad AS's Sandwich
places.address: Bad AS's Sandwich, 207 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5819, United States
places.description: A food truck dream from 2015 grew into a Milk District counter where sandwiches get composed, not assembled. Chef John Collazo serves the Ninja, an Asian glazed pork belly sandwich with spicy miso aioli that put the place on Orlando's food map. House built sandwiches land on French rolls baked in house, each with crunchy kettle chips made on site. Weekly specials sell out early, and the room shares its address with a bike shop. Choose Bad AS's Sandwich when you want a regular's club feel and a sandwich that eats like a full composition.

places.name: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe
places.address: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe, 1181 Rinehart Rd, Sanford, FL 32771-7390, United States
places.description: Mom's recipes run Dali's, and you can taste the family in every bite. This small Sanford spot serves Lao and Thai cooking built on fresh ingredients and generous portions, from homemade sausage with sticky rice and fiery jaew bong pepper paste to the red curry chicken noodle soup regulars order on repeat. The pad thai and papaya salad get raved about, the curry beef empanadas sell themselves, and takeout orders arrive with sweet handwritten notes. Come for flavor, not frills, and you will not miss the frills at all.

places.name: Taqueria las Cazuelas
places.address: Taqueria las Cazuelas, 10360 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4364, United States
places.description: A beloved Eastside story starts with the original Las Cazuelas, which built a devoted following on authentic home-style Mexican cooking. The family opened this taco-centric outpost on East Colonial, and the magic carried over. Tacos come double-wrapped in soft corn tortillas with onion and cilantro: birria, carne asada, al pastor and carnitas, with a house red sauce that regulars warn is potent. Weekend menudo keeps the loyalists coming back, and every plate tastes like a kitchen that genuinely loves feeding you. It is the East Colonial stop for home-style tacos without pretense.

places.name: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana
places.address: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana, 5475 Gateway Village Cir, Orlando, FL 32812-4002, United States
places.description: Family owned since 1998, Agave Azul gives Mexican cooking a stylized, high energy night out. Tortillas are hand pressed fresh, churrasco comes off the fire smoky, and the margarita program becomes the show with pours like Clase Aparte and Night in Tulum. Birria tacos, queso fundido with chorizo and jalapenos rellenos round out a menu that never phones in flavor. Loud in the best way, the Milk District room suits a group. Come when dinner should feel like the start of the night.

places.name: Delaney's Tavern
places.address: Delaney's Tavern, 1315 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: On the ground floor of the boutique Delaney Hotel, this SoDo tavern has been the neighborhood's special-occasion answer since 2019, and it earned the reputation honestly.
